name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 9 August 2003

date.source: The bracket date in the posted subject lines ("[08.09.03]"); the broadcast's own opening commentary places it after UWF Gold Rush 2003.

matches.how: Sierra Browne pinned Leslie Hernandez with a split-legged facebuster.

evidence.note: Non-title women's singles match, first bout of the card.

matches.how: Paul Wong retained the UWF Rampage Championship when Tom Landis was disqualified after Trevor Hextall broke up a pinfall attempt; Team Canada (Hextall and Bob Jablonski) then beat down Wong and his partner Simon O'Neal until Alex Kidd ran in for the save.

evidence.note: For the UWF Rampage Championship.

matches.how: Chris O'Brien pinned champion Uriah Hawkins with a moonsault to win the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World, after Hawkins broke his arm on a botched fall.

evidence.note: Advertised as a Cruiserweight Championship of the World defense against "Iconoclast" Sean Watts, who no-showed with an injury; Chris O'Brien volunteered from the crowd as a same-night replacement challenger. For the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World.

matches.how: Ruled a no-contest after Serge Annis's interference let Cameron Black flee the ring before a fall; Annis then chokeslammed both Papa Legba and his manager Tigress.

evidence.note: No formal decision was ever rendered; the referee never made a count.

matches.how: Tragedy pinned Derek Irvin with a belly-to-belly overhead brainbuster (the Sleepy Hollow Driver).

evidence.note: Non-title singles match.

matches.how: Ruled a no-contest and thrown out after a mass brawl spilled outside the ring, drawing in the Sons of Cacophony, the Romanis, Scott Daniels, and Tom Landis; champions the Ghost Dancers (Jason and Michael Keening) retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship by default.

evidence.note: Main event three-way dance for the UWF World Tag Team Championship.

notes: Parts served: Hour One, Hour Two Part 1, Hour Two Part 2. The show closes on a non-match angle: newly-crowned World Heavyweight Champion Edmond Winston IV stages an in-ring celebration that turns into an ambush of Michael Augustine with a rigged, glass-shard-loaded replica title belt. "Iconoclast" Sean Watts was advertised for the Cruiserweight Championship defense but did not appear, reported injured; he is not a match participant.

date.source: The bracket date in the posted subject lines ("[08.30]"); the broadcast follows directly from the prior week's Rampage in Atlanta.

evidence.note: For the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World. Marissa Monet served as a guest color commentator for the match and did not compete.

matches.how: Vyolynce forced the referee to stop the match with a dragon sleeper and body scissors combination after Randall Osbourne went unconscious.

matches.how: Tom Landis exposed a turnbuckle pad to hit Alex Kidd with a Crossed-Arms Bomb, and Scott Daniels pinned Quinn Brown with the Before the Fall piledriver after a low blow.

evidence.note: Dream Partners tag team main event, non-title.

notes: Parts served: Hour One, Hour Two. Serge Annis, Derek Irvin, Chris O'Brien, Tara Marshall, Erin McCoys, Marissa Monet, and Tawni Northern appear in angles or as guest commentators on this card but do not compete in a structured match.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 November 2003

date.source: The bracket date on the posted opening graphics ("11-15-2003"), which also label the three posted parts Hour One Part 1, Hour One Part 2, and Hour Two; the broadcast's own commentary places the show at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada.

matches.how: The One-Winged Angel connected with a top-rope moonsault elbowdrop (Hell's Halo) for the pin after manager Virginia St. Ursula distracted Brian McKenzie with a bottle of Bailey's Irish Cream at ringside.

evidence.note: UWF Rampage Championship defense; the champion retains.

matches.how: Lisa Drake rolled Leanna Love up from behind for the pin moments after Tara Marshall ran in from the crowd and knocked out Leanna's cornerwoman, Lolita Love, with the ring steps.

evidence.note: Women's contest, non-title; the UWF Women's Tag Team Championship was not at stake in this singles match.

matches.how: Niklos Romani twisted a springboard flipping neckbreaker into a swinging DDT on Brian McKenzie for the pin, back in the ring after the brawl had spilled through the MGM Grand's bar, lobby, and backstage hallways.

evidence.note: Las Vegas Street Fight (pinfall or submission must happen in the ring, otherwise anything goes) between the Fraternity Boys and the Arcana; Virginia St. Ursula and Michael Bonn handcuffed Chris O'Brien to the crowd barrier partway through, keeping him out of the finish.

matches.how: Scott Daniels used a low blow behind the referee's back and put his feet on the ropes for extra leverage on the Pridebreaker pin.

evidence.note: Singles contest, non-title. Afterward Daniels challenged Quinn Brown to a sixty-minute Iron Man match at Eve of Destruction.

matches.how: Serge Annis caught Youth Gone Wild on a reversed suplex attempt and drove him down neck-first with a throat-toss Epitomizer chokeslam for the pin.

evidence.note: Billed as a "Singles War" against Cameron Black, who appeared only by satellite from another city to announce he would not show up; no bell was ever rung for that pairing, and it is not structured as a match. Youth Gone Wild answered Annis's open in-ring challenge instead, opening the match, and busted Annis open with a top-rope DDT reversal before losing.

matches.how: Stephanie Harper forced Donna Tetreault to tap out to a center-ring Texas Cloverleaf.

evidence.note: UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World defense; the champion retains. Vice-President Jessica Marshall barred Tetreault's trainer, Simon O'Neal, from ringside beforehand.

matches.how: Michael Keening hit a moonsault press on Trevor Hextall and Edward Drake in the bottom cell, then he and his brother Jason Keening both climbed out of the tower, completing their side's escape first. Erik Grimsson had been the first individual out of the cage, but Sabbat Justice (the Arcana, Vyolynce, and Avanter) ambushed him on the arena floor and kept his brother Chad from following until well into the match; the tag stipulation went to whichever complete pair escaped first, which turned out to be the Grimssons.

evidence.note: Main event Tower of Doom cage-escape match, the UWF North American Tag Team Championship on the line for whichever complete tag team escaped first; the Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) won the belts away from their own side's champions, the Ghost Dancers (the Keening brothers), who escaped afterward.

notes: Parts served: three posts (Hour One Part 1, Hour One Part 2, Hour Two). World Champion Edmond Winston IV was ambushed in the parking lot before the show by Michael Augustine and Allison Ivey, who axed and torched his limousine with him inside; no bell was rung and it is not structured as a match. Winston later met privately with Edward and Jacob Drake, offering an alliance and a mysterious envelope about the UWF's own power structure. Alex Extreme was found backstage in a dressing-room meeting with Allison Ivey and Michael Augustine, unresolved on this page. Sarah Reed's own condition after her reported backstage attack was not addressed on this page.

name: UWF Meltdown, 17 December 2003

date.source: The broadcast's own opening graphics date and place it: "December 17th, 2003 - Family Arena - St. Charles, MO."

matches.stipulation: fifteen-man battle royal, seeding the Meltdown Championship tournament's four semi-finalists
matches.note: Victor Frost won, throwing Paul Wong with a Samoan drop for the final elimination. Rage was the first man out, clobbered from behind by Simon O'Neal; Eugene Robinson followed, flipped to the floor by Paul Wong. Several further eliminations went unannounced by name before Brian McKenzie was skinned-the-cat over the top by Alex Kidd, and Tom Landis was thrown out next by Cameron Black. Alex Kidd and Tragedy both fell together when Avanter snapmared Kidd into him; Avanter himself then went over the top under his own weight as Cameron Black kept up the pressure, and Black immediately followed Avanter to the floor and left through the crowd rather than continue. That left the final four, in their own elimination order: Tigress, Papa Legba, Victor Frost (the battle royal's own winner), and Paul Wong (the last man eliminated). Legba speared Wong into a corner; Wong backdropped Legba to the floor; Tigress attacked Frost before Wong eliminated her; Frost then Samoan-dropped Wong for the win.

matches.how: The masked Fantasy Girl pinned "Mystical" Mitzi Sukkora with a top-rope moonsault press in her in-ring debut.

evidence.note: Ladies debut match; Fantasy Girl's identity was not revealed.

matches.how: Ravnos Romani caught Todd Franklin in a small package for the pin just short of the Arcana's own corner; as the referee counted, Niklos Romani leapt off his brother's shoulders to plant a forearm in Bobby Lincoln's face and keep him from breaking it up.

evidence.note: Non-title tag team contest, the Universal Powers (Todd Franklin, Bobby Lincoln) against the Arcana.

matches.how: Paul Wong caught Tigress in midair off a Tiger Pounce attempt and drilled her with a Samoan drop for the pin, advancing to the finals.

evidence.note: Meltdown Championship tournament semi-final.

matches.how: Papa Legba countered a one-handed facelock attempt from an injured Victor Frost with a powerbomb into the turnbuckles, then finished him with an inverted DDT for the pin, advancing to the finals.

evidence.note: Meltdown Championship tournament semi-final.

matches.how: Lolita Love reversed Tara Marshall's Ray of Sunshine submission hold into a rollup for the pin.

evidence.note: Women's contest, non-title.

matches.how: Papa Legba scissored Paul Wong off a superplex attempt and drove him into the mat with the Black Magic superbomb for the pin, becoming the first-ever UWF Meltdown Champion.

evidence.note: Main event, finals of the tournament Commissioner Becky Byers announced the previous week to crown the promotion's first-ever champion. UWF Meltdown Championship, first-ever reign.

notes: Parts served: single post. Opened with Commissioner Becky Byers presenting the newly-commissioned Meltdown Championship belt before the battle royal. Papa Legba's Sabbat Justice stablemates, Tigress and Avanter, discussed his motive for entering the tournament backstage beforehand. The Romani brothers discussed a future UWF North American Tag Team Championship challenge against the Sons of Cacaphony backstage. "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee delivered an in-ring promo responding to Jessica "Fatality" Marshall. Edward and Jacob Drake met privately with World Champion Edmond Winston IV again, with Edward increasingly persuaded to the alliance; that thread continues on this wing's own 20 December 2003 page.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 20 December 2003

date.source: The posted parts' own opening graphics date the show "12-17-2003" and "12-20-2003" inconsistently, but the commentary places it at the Kemper Arena in Kansas City, Missouri, the week after the 17 December 2003 Meltdown; this collection dates the broadcast to Saturday 20 December 2003, matching the later graphic and the posted subject line.

matches.how: The One-Winged Angel pinned Scott "Hotspot" Daniels with the Revelator after Quinn Brown's entrance music distracted Daniels, who had just scored an unofficial pinfall of his own moments after knocking out the referee.

evidence.note: UWF Rampage Championship defense; the champion retains. Quinn Brown ran in afterward with a baseball bat to attack Daniels and challenge him to an Iron Man match at Eve of Destruction.

matches.how: Sierra Browne caught Tara Smith with a superkick for the pin after Smith survived four straight moonsaults, the fourth into raised knees.

evidence.note: Women's contest, non-title. Marissa Monet interrupted afterward to declare herself Stephanie Harper's challenger for the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World at Eve of Destruction, only for Sierra Browne to reveal she had already signed that contract herself; Tara Smith then challenged Monet to a singles match at the same show.

matches.how: A still-staggering Cameron Black, freshly ambushed backstage by Serge Annis, knocked Collision Holly out cold with a single right hand before the referee could even call for the bell to be rung again after the count-in.

evidence.note: Singles match, non-title. Serge Annis had appeared on the Unitron to taunt Black over an implied threat to Sasha Ellison, then ambushed him with a lead pipe as he stood in the ring; the beatdown is not itself structured as a match.

matches.how: Chris O'Brien stumbled into an Ace Crusher counter as Quinn Brown came off the middle rope for his own inverted DDT, and the champion fell on top of Brown for the pin.

evidence.note: UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World defense; the champion retains. Michael Bonn interrupted the pre-match introductions by beating a captive Brian McKenzie on the production truck's camera and challenging O'Brien to a backstage fight; the two brawled through the arena for the rest of the broadcast, ending with Bonn piledriving O'Brien onto a steel chair in the lobby.

matches.how: Angel applied the Altar of Fire submission hold to a barely-conscious Nina Grimsson, who was coughing up blood after Avanter drove her down twice with a full-nelson suplex and a full-nelson backbreaker; the referee stopped the match.

evidence.note: Intergender tag team contest, non-title. Nina Grimsson was taken to a local hospital for observation afterward.

matches.how: A twelve-man elimination match: a wrestler was eliminated by pinfall, submission, count-out, or disqualification, and his side's survivors would pick their own stipulations for Eve of Destruction. Eliminated in order: Erik Grimsson, pinned by Bob Jablonski after Kari Stevens's illegal hockey-stick shot; Bob Jablonski, pinned by Edmond Winston IV's Cobra Clutch suplex, stealing the fall from his own teammate Chad Grimsson; Edward Drake, submitting to Michael Augustine's Path of Bones nervehold; Trevor Hextall, pinned by Chad Grimsson's Rib Wrecker combination; Chad Grimsson, pinned by Michael Augustine's Impact DDT after Winston spitefully tagged an injured Grimsson back in as revenge for an earlier slight (Grimsson had been ambushed by Sabbat Justice at ringside during the match, dropped neck-first onto exposed concrete by Avanter); Michael Augustine and Edmond Winston IV together, counted out after brawling out of the arena; Kyle Lee, rolled up by Alex Extreme; Michael Keening, pinned by Jacob Drake's Gourdbuster after surviving a long string of near-falls; and finally Jacob Drake, pinned by a Hart Attack clothesline-legdrop combination from Alex Extreme and a tagged-in Jason Keening.

evidence.note: Main event, twelve-man elimination match put together by Commissioner Becky Byers and Vice-President Jessica Marshall; not a title match. Alex Extreme and Jason Keening, the last two survivors, won the right to set the stipulations for their own side's matches at Eve of Destruction, which Marshall then used to announce the full pay-per-view lineup.

notes: Parts served: three posts (Hour One, Hour Two Part 1, Hour Two Part 2). Vice-President Jessica Marshall announced the full Eve of Destruction (31 December 2003, Buffalo, New York) card at the close of the show, all future matches not structured here: Edmond Winston IV defends the World Heavyweight Championship against Michael Augustine; Quinn Brown and Scott Daniels wrestle a sixty-minute Iron Man match; Cameron Black meets Serge Annis in a Barbed Wire Match; Michael Bonn challenges Chris O'Brien for the Cruiserweight Championship; the Furies and Extreme Measures wrestle a Last Team Standing match in Detroit; Kyle Lee defends the North American Heavyweight Championship in a gauntlet against Eugene Robinson, Tragedy, and Victor Frost; Alex Kidd and Randall Osbourne meet in a First Blood Match; Stephanie Harper defends the Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World against Sierra Browne; Marissa Monet meets Tara Smith; the Bod Squad challenges the Love Sisters for the Women's Tag Team Championship; Alex Extreme and the Sons of Cacaphony face Avanter and the Arcana; and Team Canada, the Ghost Dancers, and the Privateers wrestle a three-way match for the World Tag Team Championship. Michael Bonn assaulted Brian McKenzie backstage before the Cruiserweight title match, and Cameron Black assaulted Vice-President Jessica Marshall in her office, forcing the barbed wire match against Serge Annis. Randall Osbourne attacked a returning Alex Kidd from behind again without explanation, sending him to a local hospital; Kidd's own reason for confronting Osbourne, his belief that Osbourne attacked President Sarah Reed, went unanswered again.

name: UWF Meltdown, 10 March 2004

date.source: The broadcast's own opening graphics date and place it: "March 10th, 2004 - Rexall Place - Edmonton, AB."

matches.how: Troy Grace made Job Holly submit to the Saving Grace (a Sasorigatame) in his own in-ring debut, after using his feet on the ropes for illegal leverage on an earlier pin attempt.

evidence.note: Debut match for both wrestlers.

matches.how: "Prairie Fire" Mark Marleau, a same-day replacement flown in from Saskatoon, pinned Taurus of the Heroes of Sports Entertainment with the Saskatoon Special (a roundhouse kick) in his own in-ring debut, after a late bearhug rally by Taurus.

evidence.note: Debut match for both wrestlers.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault pinned "Alluring" Arielle Starr with a bridging Domination Day suplex after "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict, brandishing a knife at ringside, distracted Starr out of a Starrstruck attempt.

evidence.note: Women's contest; Simon O'Neal coached Tetreault from ringside beforehand.

matches.how: Tigress pinned "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict with a double Sumatran Headhunter after Benedict's attention split between the match and the entrance ramp.

evidence.note: Women's contest; Marissa Monet blindsided Tigress with a Hand of God after the bell, before the referee could formally announce a winner.

matches.how: "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker pinned Youth Gone Wild with Planting Flowers for the Dead, a super implant DDT, in his own in-ring debut, after countering a springboard dropkick attempt with an elbow strike.

evidence.note: Debut match for Shay Parker.

matches.how: Scott Daniels pinned Michael Keening with a spiked Dream Catcher combination while two unidentified men in suits ambushed his own teammates Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski's opponents at ringside; the two attackers were never named and fled through the crowd afterward.

evidence.note: Six-man tag, Team Canada and Scott Daniels versus the Ghost Dancers and Erik Grimsson; an earlier phone call between Strictly Business's Mike Sebastian and an unnamed contact hinted at a hired favor but never confirmed the attackers' identity on-page.

matches.how: Papa Legba retained the UWF Meltdown Championship, pinning Alex Kidd with the Ragga Bomb after Kidd left the ring to check on wife Alicia amid a confrontation with a menacing Randall Osbourne; Tigress had softened Legba up with a mid-match rescue and a wake-up slap beforehand.

evidence.note: For the UWF Meltdown Championship.

notes: Parts served: single post. Opened with a hospital-room comedy cold open, Alex Extreme running up Edmond Winston IV's own bill out of spite; the Sons of Cacaphony and "Agony" Michael Augustine reluctantly agreed to work with Extreme against Winston's new regime. Rodney and a children's choir pranked Jessica Marshall with the Barney theme song. World Heavyweight Champion Michael Augustine cut a parking-lot promo dismissing the entire roster's threat under "Marshall Law," reserving respect only for North American Heavyweight Champion Kyle Lee. "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath, freshly returned and thrown out of the previous show, challenged Jamie Underwood to a match, interrupted by a family incident with his own children Alex Price and Anastasia. Avanter and the midget-seer Botan flew to Germany, Avanter reading his own tarot cards as a promise of vengeance against Serge Annis. Tigress and her foster sister Leslie Hernandez fell out over the Coven's own internal tensions; Simon O'Neal privately worried about Randall Osbourne threatening his own wife, Alicia Kidd. "Dead End" Derek Martin confronted Vice-President Jessica Marshall in her own office over his contract's free-reign clause. Strictly Business's Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian discussed the Ghost Dancers and Team Canada by phone, Sebastian later arranging an unspecified favor for someone unnamed. Dalbello Rage recruited Marissa Monet into a new alliance she called the Misfits, not yet named or shown in the ring. Alex Extreme closed the broadcast promising a response to Winston's "example."

name: UWF Meltdown, 21 March 2004

date.source: The broadcast's own opening graphics date and place it: "March 21st, 2004 - Prospera Place - Kelowna, B.C."

matches.how: Referee stoppage; "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict wore down Brianna Landis, sent in by Tara Marshall as a last-second substitute opponent, before locking on a DDT into leg scissors until the official called the match.

evidence.note: Women's match; Tara Marshall interfered repeatedly from the apron on her own personal assistant and sister-in-law's behalf.

matches.how: "Swinger" Troy Grace reversed a Death Valley Driver attempt into an inverted facelock and twisted it into an Ace Crusher for the pin on "Jukebox" T.D. Swagger, after both men traded eye-rakes and near-falls.

evidence.note: Debut match for T.D. Swagger, one half of Happy Hardcore.

matches.how: "Banshee" Michael Keening followed a Twisting Monster Drop (a second-rope DVD) with a top-rope somersault splash for the pin on "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker.

evidence.note: One-on-one match.

matches.how: A double uranage slam set up Sierra Browne's Showstopper legdrop to finish Fantasy Girl, despite a rescue attempt from Tesla St. James and "Alluring" Arielle Starr.

evidence.note: Six-woman tag, the in-ring debut of the Misfits (Marissa Monet, Sierra Browne, and Dalbello Rage) as a formal trio; Tigress ran in after the bell to attack Marissa Monet.

matches.how: Serge Annis pulled his own partner Caliban to safety off a Fury double-team attempt and clotheslined Spice over the top rope, and Caliban then brought Rage down with a superplex across Annis's own outstretched knee for the pin.

evidence.note: Tag match, Fury (Rage and Spice) versus the debuting pairing of Serge Annis and Caliban.

matches.how: The Sons of Cacaphony retained the UWF North American Tag Team Championship after Chad Grimsson's mammoth dive to the floor swung momentum their way, the Sky Hammer combination finishing Bobby Lincoln moments later.

evidence.note: For the UWF North American Tag Team Championship.

matches.how: Champion Papa Legba attacked both challengers with a chair before the bell ever rang, then took the microphone to announce he was too grief-stricken over his own father's recent death to defend the title, postponing the match to a steel cage bout the following week; no bout ever started and no fall was scored.

evidence.note: Main event, scheduled as a three-way dance for the UWF Meltdown Championship.

notes: Parts served: single post. A returning former cruiserweight champion, Steve Ryott, was shown in the crowd, prompting on-air speculation but no further appearance. Alex Extreme and Rodney evaded the Keening brothers backstage, trading accusations of racism over old wounds; Jason Keening broke his own on-air composure to curse at Extreme for a past attack on a fifty-year-old man. Chad Grimsson confided in brother Erik about his own recent break-up with Sonya Benedict, revealing Sonya to be Myra Benedict's cousin. Tigress, alone in her apartment, cut a promo on Marissa Monet referencing her own recent split from Sabbat Justice. Arielle Starr, Tesla St. James (introduced by mentor Kyle Lee), and Fantasy Girl each cut promos previewing their six-woman tag against the newly-formed Misfits, who answered in kind. Amity's Rage, Spice, and the One-Winged Angel traded words backstage before the Fury tag match; Serge Annis and Caliban were shown separately agreeing to disregard "Marshall Law" and destroy anyone in their way. Alex Extreme cut a pre-match promo naming Papa Legba and Randall Osbourne as obstacles rather than his real target, Edmond Winston IV. A paid, non-UWF vignette closed the broadcast: outside talent Alex Martinez threatened Scott "Hotspot" Daniels over a sneak attack, promising to attend every remaining Rampage for two months.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 24 March 2004

date.source: Hour One's own opening graphics date and place it: "03-24-2004" at the Pengrowth Saddledome, Calgary, Alberta. Hour Two's own graphics carry a conflicting "03-13-2004" date stamp, evidently a typo by the same author; Hour One's date, the Rampage following directly from the postponed 21 March 2004 Meltdown cage-match announcement and posted first in sequence, is treated as authoritative.

matches.how: Uriah Hawkins retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "Dead End" Derek Martin, catching him in a small package moments after both men traded a side Russian legsweep and a near-miss brainbuster.

evidence.note: For the UWF Rampage Championship. Martin chair-shotted Hawkins after the bell; "The Doomsayer" Kyle Lee ran him off.

matches.how: Angel pinned debuting Reona Yoshida with a reverse Ace Crusher, the Headhunter, after Yoshida injured her own shoulder missing a springboard plancha.

evidence.note: Women's contest. Angel disguised herself as her brother Vyolynce for a pre-match interview; countrywoman Misaki Ishikawa ran in to break up a post-match submission hold.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault beat "Wildfire" Leslie Hernandez by referee stoppage, applying the Caress of Steel after knocking Hernandez out cold with a ringside water bucket.

evidence.note: Women's contest. Simon O'Neal and the Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos), the wrestlers' respective cornermen, brawled throughout at ringside.

matches.how: An impromptu match between owner Edmond Winston IV and his own protege Jamie Underwood ended without a decision after Sabbath ambushed Underwood with a Singapore cane, then World Champion Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme ran in, followed by the Privateers to clear them out.

evidence.note: Winston first offered Underwood a staged win, then turned on him for real once he accepted it. Winston announced a handicap main event, the Youngbloods against his own New Era, for the following Rampage.

matches.how: A non-title cruiserweight match between Michael Bonn and newcomer November was ruled a double disqualification after Jamie Underwood attacked November and the One-Winged Angel entered the ring to help fend him off.

evidence.note: The One-Winged Angel appeared in street clothes with his trademark cane, taking part in the ringside brawl before the finish.

matches.how: Alex Kidd and wife Alicia Powers beat Tom Landis and wife Tara Marshall in a husband-and-wife intergender tag match, Kidd's own Somersault Bulldog on Landis clearing the way for Powers's pinfall.

evidence.note: President Jessica Marshall made the match intergender on the spot. Randall Osbourne brought out Alex Kidd's own ex-wife, Cameo, after the bell; she low-blowed Kidd and hairpulled Powers down before leaving with Osbourne.

matches.how: Victor Frost retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over "Screaming Drillbit" Jason Keening, pinning him with a Death Valley Driver after blinding him with fingerpaint smuggled in by manager Simone Sumner.

evidence.note: Main event, for the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship.

notes: Parts served: Hour One, Hour Two. Erik and Chad Grimsson (with Alex Extreme and Rodney) gave owner Edmond Winston IV a mocking golden garden-gnome statue of himself as a housewarming gift. Sonya Benedict ambushed Nina Grimsson backstage with a chair. Misaki Ishikawa, Kari Stevens, Simon O'Neal, the Amazing Romanis, Simone Sumner, Roxy Mayhem, Erika Lima, Rodney, Sabbath, Michael Augustine, Alex Extreme, the Privateers, Randall Osbourne, and Cameo (Alex Kidd's returning ex-wife) all appear in angles or backstage segments but do not compete in a structured match on this card. Randall Osbourne was originally advertised in a steel-cage main event but does not appear on this page; the cage rematch runs on the next UWF Meltdown broadcast.

name: UWF Meltdown, 5 May 2004

date.source: The broadcast's own opening graphics date and place it: "May 5th, 2004 - Denver Coliseum - Denver, CO."

matches.how: Debuting Brazilian cruiserweight Scorpio pinned Collision Holly with a top-rope frog splash, the Brazilian Bomb.

evidence.note: Singles debut match. Scorpio was accompanied by manager and girlfriend Erika Lima.

matches.how: November pinned a returning Pierce Bleed with a tornado DDT, extending his own unbeaten UWF start.

evidence.note: Bleed's own return from the suspended list, arranged by tag partner T.D. Swagger.

matches.how: Kari Stevens pinned "Mystical" Mitzi Sukkora with a corkscrew 450 splash in her own forced-through in-ring debut.

evidence.note: Stevens demanded the match from Commissioner Becky Byers earlier in the show.

matches.how: "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict pinned "Wildfire" Leslie Hernandez with her feet on the ropes after a superkick counter to a charging spear.

evidence.note: Women's match. Benedict applied a post-match Morbid Sting until Arielle Starr ran in and traded blows with her.

matches.how: A scrambled-partners tag pairing Michael Keening with Erik Grimsson against a reluctant pairing of Niklos Romani and Todd Franklin was called a no-contest after Franklin turned on his own partner, chokeslamming and lariating him before finishing Grimsson with a New Horizon Line.

evidence.note: Franklin and Bobby Lincoln (not on this card) vowed afterward to injure the top tag teams in the promotion.

matches.how: Nina Grimsson beat "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict by disqualification after Benedict busted her open with a fluorescent light tube found under the ring.

evidence.note: Tesla St. James and Lisa Drake ran in to pull Benedict off; both stayed backstage before the match at Grimsson's own request and do not otherwise appear in this card's matches.

matches.how: "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker pinned "Prairie Fire" Mark Marleau with an uppercut knockout after methodically working over his knee.

evidence.note: One-on-one match.

matches.how: Papa Legba retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Alex Extreme, climbing out of the steel cage to the arena floor first after knocking Extreme off the top of the cage.

evidence.note: Main event, rescheduled from the 21 March 2004 no-contest, for the UWF Meltdown Championship. Randall Osbourne, the match's own third advertised participant, never entered the cage after Alex Kidd attacked him at ringside before the bell.

notes: Parts served: single post. Kari Stevens forced Commissioner Becky Byers into giving her an in-ring debut. Lisa Drake, Tesla St. James, and Nina Grimsson (of Extreme Measure) planned Grimsson's own solo response to Sonya Benedict backstage; the Love Sisters (Leanna and Lolita Love) returned from a layoff to challenge tag champions the Bod Squad and to call out Nina Grimsson on Leanna's own behalf. Bobby Lincoln appeared with brother Todd Franklin in a parking-lot promo threatening the promotion's top tag teams; "Dead End" Derek Martin cut a promo threatening Kyle Lee; Shay Parker cut a promo threatening Mark Marleau ahead of their match. "Agony" Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme announced the reformation of the Youngbloods against Edmond Winston IV's New Era for the following Rampage's handicap main event. Pierce Bleed threw the physical Meltdown Championship belt into the crowd during the main event, then firebombed Edmond Winston IV's parked limousine after the show; neither act was structured as a match.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 May 2004

date.source: Hour One's own opening graphics date it "05-15-2004" at Denver's Pepsi Center; the subject line both parts were posted under reads "[05.05]," but 5 May 2004 was a Wednesday (the same date the held record's prior Meltdown already aired) while 15 May 2004 was a Saturday, matching the show's own "Saturday Night Rampage" title and this wing's standing Wednesday-Meltdown/Saturday-Rampage pattern; the internal graphic is treated as authoritative and the subject line as a copied-forward typo.

matches.how: Uriah Hawkins retained the UWF Rampage Championship in a three-way dance, sneaking in behind both challengers as they collided and catching them together with a double DDT for the pin.

evidence.note: For the UWF Rampage Championship. Troy Grace and Quinn Brown traded numerous near-falls on each other throughout, including a Grace fisherman's suplex and a Brown superkick, before Hawkins's late double DDT ended it.

matches.how: A six-man tag between Alex Kidd, Paul Wong, and "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee and Team Canada's Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski with "Hotspot" Scott Daniels ended without a decision when stablemate Tom Landis and the debuting Alex Martinez both entered the ring to brawl with each other; unable to tell who had entered first, the referee called for the bell with the match still undecided.

evidence.note: Kari Stevens accompanied Daniels, Hextall, and Jablonski to the ring but did not compete. The finish escalated into a mass brawl involving Alex Martinez, November, the Ghost Dancers, Serge Annis, Caliban, Randall Osbourne, Cameo, "Dead End" Derek Martin, and Alicia Powers; none of them are structured as match participants.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault won the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World, hurling herself over the top rope with a somersault plancha onto both Stephanie Harper and cornerman Simon O'Neal, then dragging the barely-conscious champion back into the ring for the pinfall as the referee's ten count on both women lapsed.

evidence.note: For the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World. O'Neal interfered from the apron repeatedly during the match; a pair of brass knuckles was found at ringside after the bell, though no one openly claimed them.

matches.how: A four-on-two handicap main event dissolved into chaos with no fall ever scored: the Privateers, Edward and Jacob Drake, turned on partner Edmond Winston IV mid-match to side with Alex Extreme, triple-conchairtoing Winston and putting him through a table, only for Michael Augustine to then turn on Extreme himself, and the Privateers and Augustine beat Extreme through a second table before Alex Martinez and the Sons of Cacaphony ran in to pull him clear as the broadcast ran out of time.

evidence.note: Main event. Jamie Underwood was thrown from the ring early by Michael Augustine and took no further part. Rodney, Alex Extreme's non-competing companion, was briefly held hostage by the Privateers during the beatdown.

notes: Parts served: Hour One, Hour Two. Kari Stevens, Tom Landis, Alex Martinez (in his own debut appearance in the held record), November, the Ghost Dancers (Jason and Michael Keening), Serge Annis, Caliban, Randall Osbourne, Cameo, "Dead End" Derek Martin, Alicia Powers, and the Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) all appear in the six-man tag's own closing brawl or the main event's own aftermath but do not compete in a structured match on this card. Backstage, Derek Martin and Tesla St. James clashed with Kyle Lee, who agreed to a Gold Rush street fight against Martin. Angel delivered a lengthy dark-room promo naming several women's-division rivals. Victor Frost terrorized Quinn Brown's manager Victoria Marquess backstage; Brown chased Frost to the parking garage without catching him. Sabbath confronted Jamie Underwood over a custody scheme against his children, assaulting him before being restrained. Serge Annis and Caliban attacked and hospitalized Paul Wong in his own locker room after the six-man tag; Alex Kidd and Kyle Lee carried him out for medical help, both citing the lack of on-site security under owner Edmond Winston IV's "Marshall Law" policy.

name: UWF Meltdown, 19 May 2004

date.source: The broadcast's own opening graphics date and place it: "May 19th, 2004 - Allstate Arena - Chicago, IL."

matches.how: "Battle Princess" Misaki Ishikawa beat Fantasy Girl in an interpromotional attraction match, hooking the leg of her own Skull Crash Buster for the pin.

evidence.note: Billed UWF versus Project BATTLE*DREAM; Ishikawa was accompanied by sidekick Rocko and carried a taser to the ring, though it went unused in the match itself.

matches.how: The Universal Powers beat the Harlequins, Todd Franklin and Bobby Lincoln finishing Terror with the Universal Elimination after an unidentified well-dressed man ringside felled Chaos with a mafia kick.

evidence.note: Niklos Romani ambushed both Universal Powers members with a chair before the bell, at storyline Ravnos Romani's own goading; the same well-dressed man had assaulted Harlequin Tragedy backstage earlier in the broadcast and is not identified on this page.

matches.how: Alicia Powers won her own in-ring singles debut, scooping up "Alluring" Arielle Starr after her leg buckled mid-suplex and finishing her with a Michinoku Driver.

evidence.note: Singles debut match. The two competitors shook hands before and after.

matches.how: "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict was awarded the win by disqualification over "British Bad Girl" Lisa Drake after Nina Grimsson and Tesla St. James ran in and beat Benedict unconscious with Drake's own Singapore cane.

evidence.note: Women's contest. Grimsson and St. James left the ring to loud cheers once Benedict was down and bleeding.

matches.how: "The Savior" Jamie Underwood beat Chad Grimsson by pinfall, shifting his weight onto a charging Grimsson for a rollup while Sonya Benedict held Grimsson's own leg down from ringside.

evidence.note: Singles bout. Underwood tended to a still-recovering Sonya Benedict at ringside before the bell.

matches.how: The One-Winged Angel won a four corners contenders match for the number-one contendership to the UWF Cruiserweight Championship, lifting T.D. Swagger into a Revelator and driving him down across the other two fallen men for the pin.

evidence.note: Winner earns a UWF Cruiserweight Championship match against Michael Bonn at Gold Rush. The bout spilled outside the ring repeatedly; all four competitors celebrated together afterward.

matches.how: "Dead End" Derek Martin beat "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker by pinfall, ducking a straight punch and snapping Parker down with an inverted ace crusher.

evidence.note: One-on-one match.

matches.how: Papa Legba retained the UWF Meltdown Championship, teaming with Tigress to beat Simon O'Neal and Donna Tetreault after a top-rope splash caught both opponents at once for the pin.

evidence.note: Main event, intergender tag for the UWF Meltdown Championship. Both sides used a pair of brass knuckles and a handful of black-and-gold powder over the course of the match; the referee was blinded by the powder at one point.

notes: Parts served: single post. Edward and Jacob Drake announced from a locker room that they and Michael Augustine and Allison Ivey had purchased minority shares of the UWF, using them to lock in the stipulations of their own future matches; Edmond Winston IV replied with a chess-themed office monologue naming Serge Annis and Caliban as the instrument of his own revenge. "Pit Monster" Chad Grimsson traded threats with ex-girlfriend Sonya Benedict backstage before their partners' matches. Alex Martinez confronted hospital staff and Erik and Chad Grimsson while waiting on Alex Extreme's condition, patching up a prior grievance with Chad. Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian (Strictly Business), hospitalized after a Team Canada attack, refused on camera to come out of retirement for Gold Rush. Harlequin Tragedy was assaulted and left unconscious backstage by an unidentified well-dressed man, the same man who later interfered in the tag match; the other Harlequins found him but the attacker was not identified. Nina Grimsson and Tesla St. James discussed Sonya Benedict and Leanna Love backstage. "Money Driven" T.D. Swagger delivered a comedic talent-show promo to tag partner Pierce Bleed (not appearing on this card) about their Gold Rush cruiserweight title opportunity. "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn, the reigning UWF Cruiserweight Champion, was talked out of scouting his Gold Rush challengers by manager Virginia St. Ursula; he does not compete on this card. Tara Marshall and sister-in-law Brianna Landis, the Women's Tag Team Champions, cut a promo declining to defend the title on the broadcast. Chris O'Brien and a visibly drunk Victor Frost shared a strip-club scene ahead of their own Gold Rush match. Tigress ate takeout in her hotel room while discussing Simon O'Neal and Donna Tetreault with her pet tiger. Simon O'Neal and Stephanie Harper argued backstage over the previous card's brass-knuckles finish.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 29 May 2004

date.source: Both articles' own opening graphics date the broadcast "05-29-2004"; the subject line both parts were posted under also reads "[05.29.04]", with no conflict this time. 29 May 2004 was a Saturday, matching the show's own "Saturday Night Rampage" title.

matches.how: Uriah Hawkins's UWF Rampage Championship defense against Tragedy was ruled a no-contest after Pierce Bleed attacked the referee with a chair while Tragedy still had the Tragic Ending locked on Hawkins near the ropes.

evidence.note: For the UWF Rampage Championship. Bleed then challenged Hawkins to a title-versus-career match at Gold Rush, naming T.D. Swagger (his own tag partner) as special referee; Hawkins accepted and speared Bleed off the middle rope as the segment closed. Tragedy's manager and wife, Comedy, accompanied him to ringside without competing.

matches.how: Kari Stevens beat Angel by pinfall in a women's match, avoiding a hotshot attempt to hook Angel's legs and ride her to the canvas for the three count.

evidence.note: Angel HeadHunter-clotheslined a recovering Stevens after the bell, unaffected by the loss.

matches.how: Serge Annis and Caliban, billed the Hands of Death, beat the Fraternity Boys (Chris O'Brien and Brian McKenzie) in a tag confrontation, Caliban catching McKenzie on an outstretched knee off a Near Death Experience superplex for the pin.

evidence.note: Billed on the card as a confrontation rather than a formal match, though both sides were legal and a referee counted the fall. O'Brien broke a Jalapeño Pepper Beer bottle over Caliban's head mid-match; Annis and Caliban kept attacking O'Brien after the bell until Jason and Michael Keening ran in for the save.

matches.how: Jason and Michael Keening's tag match against Serge Annis and Caliban ended in a double countout after both teams kept brawling outside the ring past the referee's count.

evidence.note: The Privateers ran in on the ensuing brawl; commissioner Becky Byers used the moment to add the Ghost Dancers to the already-set Gold Rush UWF World Tag Team Championship match, making it a three-way between the champion Privateers, the Ghost Dancers, and Annis and Caliban.

matches.how: Chris O'Brien, substituting for an injured Brian McKenzie, beat UWF North American Heavyweight Champion Victor Frost by countout after Frost abandoned the match to chase down a returning Quinn Brown; the title did not change hands. finish: countout

evidence.note: Frost and Brown brawled to the back and later fought in a parking garage, ending with Frost thrown through the windshield of his own car. Frost is billed here as champion, though no surviving document in the held record records how he won the title from its prior holder, Kyle Lee.

matches.how: Team Canada beat Alex Extreme and debuting Alex Martinez, Bob Jablonski pinning an exhausted, unconscious Martinez after Trevor Hextall legdropped a would-be saving Extreme.

evidence.note: Tom Landis and Kari Stevens ambushed Martinez in the aisle before the bell, busting him open with a chair and knocking him out cold before he ever tagged in; Martinez briefly rallied on his own before collapsing from exhaustion, and Scott Daniels, on commentary, ordered the pin. Erik and Chad Grimsson ran in for the save but were fought off; Daniels and Landis then Pride-broke Extreme's cornerman Rodney.

matches.how: Kyle Lee beat Edmond Winston IV by pinfall (Gone to Texas) with World Heavyweight Champion Michael Augustine as special guest referee, earning himself a spot in the Gold Rush main event triple threat against Augustine and Winston for the World Heavyweight Championship.

evidence.note: Augustine gave Winston a fair count for most of the match before decking him with a punch after Winston struck the referee. "Dead End" Derek Martin blindsided Lee with the End (an inverted ace crusher) immediately after the bell.

notes: Parts served: Hour One, Hour Two. Edmond Winston IV, Jamie Underwood, and Jessica "Fatality" Marshall discussed the Privateers' ongoing buyout of UWF ownership shares before the Pride (Scott Daniels, Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski, Tom Landis, and Kari Stevens) broke into Winston's office to threaten him over his handling of Michael Augustine and Alex Martinez; Winston vowed revenge on the Pride, the Youngbloods, and the Privateers alike. The Youngbloods (Michael Augustine, Allison Ivey, and the Privateers, Edward and Jacob Drake) mocked hometown hero Alex Extreme on their way to the ring; Augustine cut a long open-mic promo belittling Chicago and the roster before "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee interrupted him, and Jessica Marshall announced that if Lee could beat Edmond Winston IV later that night, he would join Augustine and Winston in the Gold Rush main event for the World Heavyweight Championship. Pierce Bleed ambushed Uriah Hawkins backstage over a locker-room confrontation from the previous card; T.D. Swagger and the fan group H.O.S.E. broke up the fight. Paul Wong told Simon O'Neal he would handle Serge Annis and Caliban his own way and revealed a Gold Rush stipulation for Donna Tetreault's rematch against Stephanie Harper: Wong and O'Neal would be handcuffed together at ringside. Angel pressed Jessica Marshall backstage for a Gold Rush match against Allison Ivey. Victor Frost's valet Roxy Mayhem taunted Quinn Brown before Frost, on tape delay, was shown attacking Brown's manager Victoria Marquess backstage and then ambushing Brown himself with a chair before his own title match. A returning Steve Ryott announced he wanted to reform Legion with Youth Gone Wild and Alex Kidd, recruiting a bewildered Moe Owens to gather signatures. Randall Osbourne and his manager Cameo (Alex Kidd's ex-wife) challenged Alex Kidd to a Gold Rush match; Kidd accepted after accusing Cameo of manipulating Osbourne from the start. Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian (Strictly Business) staged a wheelchair-bound retirement announcement, were mocked by Team Canada, then revealed the ruse by attacking Hextall and Jablonski and challenging Team Canada to a Gold Rush match. Jamie Underwood won a custody hearing against Sabbath and his wife Sayaka over their two children, taunting them until Sabbath assaulted him and his lawyer's security; Sabbath challenged Underwood to a Gold Rush match before losing custody. After the Extreme/Martinez tag match, Team Canada, Tom Landis, and Kari Stevens continued beating down Alex Extreme; Erik and Chad Grimsson (the Sons of Cacophony) ran in but were overwhelmed, and Scott Daniels and Landis went on to Pride-break Extreme's cornerman Rodney before Extreme rallied briefly against Daniels and Landis. Victor Frost and Quinn Brown's post-match brawl continued into a parking garage, ending with Frost thrown through the windshield of his own car.

name: UWF Gold Rush 2004

date.source: All four parts' own opening graphics and card banners date the broadcast "Live! Saturday June 5th 2004"; 5 June 2004 was a Saturday, matching the graphic.

matches.how: Angel beat Allison Ivey by pinfall (HeadHunter, an inverted clothesline) in the Gold Rush 2004 opener.

evidence.note: Ivey's own in-ring debut, managing the Youngbloods; Edward Drake of the Privateers came to ringside during the match. After the bell, Ivey and Drake chairshotted the fallen Angel twice.

matches.how: Jamie Underwood beat Sabbath by pinfall in a no-disqualification match after Sabbath's own son, Alex Price, turned on his father with a low blow and held down the cover.

evidence.note: Sabbath's first match back since August 2003 and first UWF match since February 2002, wrestling over his own custody dispute with Underwood; Underwood used his own son Alex as a hostage mid-match before Alex, planted beforehand, turned on Sabbath at the finish.

matches.how: Arielle Starr beat Myra Benedict by pinfall (Starrstruck, a top-rope Skytwister Press), countering a second Shadow's Bane kick attempt with the Bedazzler enzuigiri first.

evidence.note: Tara Smith accompanied Starr to ringside without competing.

matches.how: Kyle Lee beat "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall (Gone to Texas, a top-rope tiger driver through a table) in a street fight.

evidence.note: Falls-count-anywhere rules; both men traded steel steps, a chair, a lead pipe, and a table across a lengthy brawl. Lee's own submission hold, the Bastard Grinder, forced Martin to the ropes but did not finish him.

matches.how: Uriah Hawkins retained the UWF Rampage Championship, pinning Pierce Bleed with a Suicide DDT after special referee T.D. Swagger restarted the match, having ruled out an illegal cordless-microphone shot Bleed used for an earlier pinfall.

evidence.note: A title-versus-contract match under closed-door rules with Bleed's own tag partner, T.D. Swagger, as special referee; Bleed's UWF contract was voided under the match's own stipulation. Hawkins offered a handshake after the match, which Bleed accepted.

matches.how: Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) beat Team Canada (Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski) by pinfall, Tucker hitting a top-rope Frog Splash (the Flash N' Cash) on Hextall.

evidence.note: Strictly Business staged a wheelchair-bound retirement announcement before the match, mocked by Team Canada, then revealed the ruse and challenged Team Canada on the spot; manager Kari Stevens interfered repeatedly for Team Canada during the bout.

matches.how: Alex Kidd beat Randall Osbourne by pinfall with a full nelson bulldog.

evidence.note: A personal grudge match complicated by Osbourne's manager, Cameo, Kidd's own ex-wife; Osbourne bit open Kidd's forehead in a Tree of Woe and hit two Somersault Bulldog-style reversals, the first of which knocked Cameo herself unconscious on the outside.

matches.how: One-Winged Angel won the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World from Michael Bonn by pinfall, reversing Bonn's own Deadfall attempt into an uranage and finishing with a top-rope Hell's Halo (moonsault elbow).

evidence.note: Cornerwoman Ami Tran and Amity stablemate Spice each interfered at ringside; Bonn's manager Virginia St. Ursula was accidentally struck during the match. Bonn demanded a rematch backstage afterward while destroying his own locker room.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over Stephanie Harper by pinfall (Caress of Steel), using brass knuckles and then a foreign object hidden in her own bandana.

evidence.note: Both women's own cornermen, Paul Wong and Simon O'Neal, were handcuffed together at ringside for the match. After the win, O'Neal proposed marriage to Tetreault in the ring; she accepted the ring, then knocked him out cold.

matches.how: The Privateers (Edward and Jacob Drake) retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship in a three-way against the Hands of Death (Serge Annis and Caliban) and the Ghost Dancers (Jason and Michael Keening), Jacob Drake pinning Michael Keening with a diving splash (the High-Seas Shipwreck) after Edward's own gourdbuster.

evidence.note: Under the match's own stipulation, the champions could only lose the title by losing the fall themselves. Serge Annis was taken out of the match by a triple Conchairto from the Fraternity Boys (Chris O'Brien and Brian McKenzie), unrelated to either tag team; Michael Keening was left motionless after a Near Death Experience-style superplex from Annis and was taken to a hospital for a back injury after the match, his brother Jason attacked backstage by an unidentified masked man soon after. Gabriel Whitecross, the Keenings' brother-in-law, accompanied the Ghost Dancers to ringside without competing.

matches.how: Alex Martinez beat Scott "Hotspot" Daniels by pinfall with a Firebomb Chokeslam.

evidence.note: Daniels used a low blow, brass knuckles, and two steel chair shots; Martinez kicked out of a Pridebreaker before blocking a second attempt and finishing. Alex Extreme was ejected from the building by Winston-hired security before the match, over Rodney's protest.

matches.how: Victor Frost retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over Quinn Brown by pinfall (the Violator Mark II, a second-rope Death Valley Driver).

evidence.note: Brown's own manager, Victoria Marquess, shoved him off the top rope mid-comeback, then revealed a secret alliance with Frost, kissing him over Brown's fallen body after the match.

matches.how: Kyle Lee won the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World, pinning champion Michael Augustine with a second Gone to Texas in the Gold Rush main event triple threat, also involving Edmond Winston IV.

evidence.note: A mystery man calling himself Alex Extreme (later unmasked as Job Holly) tried to steer a remote-controlled blimp into the match before the real Alex Extreme appeared and struck both Winston and Augustine with a golf club, clearing the way for Lee's win; manager Tesla St. James embraced Lee in the ring afterward.

notes: The eighth annual Gold Rush, held at the Pontiac Silverdome in Detroit, ran four hours across thirteen matches. A Preview Show bulletin posted the same day was not read. Throughout the broadcast, a Fortress Fraternity riot subplot ran alongside the card: Jessica "Fatality" Marshall's own security guards had sealed off the Fortress Fraternity section (dubbed "Gulag Fraternity" by the announcers) inside the arena, and Chris O'Brien and Brian McKenzie, interviewed throughout the night by a reporter identifying himself as Jessica Marshall's own brother, eventually punched a guard and touched off a riot that let the fans inside get their own beer supply back; O'Brien and McKenzie also joined the Fraternity Boys in a triple Conchairto on Serge Annis during the tag team triple threat. Michael Bonn assaulted his own manager, Virginia St. Ursula, by accident during his title loss, then demanded she call the promotion for a rematch while destroying his own locker room; a video call ends the segment with her arranging one. Edward and Jacob Drake, the Privateers, watched the show alongside Michael Augustine and Allison Ivey as fellow minority owners of the promotion, per an announcement on an earlier show. Alex Extreme was thrown out of the arena by Winston-hired security ahead of the Martinez/Daniels match, over Rodney's protest, then returned during the main event to expose an impostor Alex Extreme (revealed as Job Holly) who had been remote-piloting a blimp reading "New Era in Professional Wrestling presents Gold Rush 2004" toward the ring on Winston's behalf; the real Extreme struck both Winston and Michael Augustine with a golf club before Kyle Lee's own win. A video recap package aired before the main event narrating the year's own build to the match, including Michael Augustine winning the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World from Edmond Winston IV at UWF Eve of Destruction, a broadcast this collection holds no primary-source card text for.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line reads "[08.24.04]" but the broadcast's own opening graphic reads "August 25th, 2004"; 24 August 2004 was a Tuesday and 25 August 2004 was a Wednesday, matching this wing's own established Wednesday date for every other Meltdown broadcast in the held record, so the graphic's own date is used.

matches.how: Collision Holly won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Papa Legba by pinfall, catching the champion with a second-rope bulldog after absorbing a long beating.

evidence.note: Legba had dismissed the match as a routine title defense against a curtain-jerker; Rampage Champion Uriah Hawkins, seconding Holly at ringside, had encouraged him beforehand to wrestle it seriously.

matches.how: Steve Ryott beat Taurus by pinfall with his own top-rope Ryott Bomb (a flying somersault legdrop) after an inverted DDT.

evidence.note: Ryott's own return to the ring, wearing a "Bring Back Legion... Ryott '04" t-shirt; a former UWF Cruiserweight Champion.

matches.how: "Dead End" Derek Martin beat Sabbath by pinfall (The End) after Sabbath missed a shooting star press.

evidence.note: Sabbath's wife Sayaka accompanied him to ringside; both men's minds were elsewhere over Sabbath's own custody loss at Gold Rush. Martin promised backstage beforehand to dismantle the UWF "piece by piece," naming Sabbath as the next piece.

matches.how: November beat "Jukebox" T.D. Swagger by pinfall with his own standing shooting star press, the Rain Dance, after a dropkick to the solar plexus.

evidence.note: A tightly-contested cruiserweight bout; Swagger raised November's arm in victory afterward.

matches.how: Alicia Powers beat Brianna Landis by pinfall with a Michinoku Driver after countering a vertical suplex attempt with a European uppercut.

evidence.note: After the bell, Tara "Sunburst" Marshall (the Unicorn) attacked the celebrating Powers and had Landis raise a tag title belt to strike her, but "Tornado" Tara Smith ran in to chase off the Bod Squad.

matches.how: "Mr. Excitement" Alex Extreme beat Tragedy by pinfall with a springboard version of his own finisher, the Extreme, after an implant DDT.

evidence.note: Tragedy's wife and manager, Comedy, accompanied him; Rodney distracted Tragedy mid-match by slapping Comedy on the rear and fleeing before she could retaliate.

matches.how: Team BATTLE*DREAM (Reona Yoshida and Misaki Ishikawa) won a four corners women's tag war, Yoshida hooking a double DDT on Melody and Lolita Love and pinning Melody for the fall.

evidence.note: Misaki Ishikawa's own first formal in-ring pairing with countrywoman Yoshida in this wing, managed at ringside by Rocko; the win earned Team BATTLE*DREAM a UWF Women's Tag Team Championship match against the Bod Squad the following week. Lisa Drake and Nina Grimsson (Extreme Measures) kept brawling with Yoshida and Ishikawa well after the bell.

matches.how: "Last American Badass" Alex Martinez beat "Dark Horse" Randall Osbourne by pinfall with a Firebomb Chokeslam.

evidence.note: Osbourne bit open Martinez's forehead in a Tree of Woe and hammered his injured shoulder, but Osbourne's manager Cameo could not distract Martinez when it mattered.

matches.how: Tom Landis and Team Canada beat Quinn Brown and Strictly Business, Landis and Trevor Hextall's own Game Misconduct heart-punch combination flooring Andrew Tucker for the pin.

evidence.note: Manager Kari Stevens tried to blind a downed Landis with a handful of salt, but Quinn Brown kicked it back into her own face; the Pride mocked Quinn Brown and Strictly Business's own Gold Rush victories on the way to the ring.

notes: The first post-Gold Rush edition of Meltdown, opening with Edmond Winston IV telling Jamie Underwood he trusted him with nothing more dangerous than a bodyguard assignment; Underwood and manager Uriah Hawkins previewed the Rampage Championship rematch to come. Michael Bonn refused comment on his own demanded Cruiserweight rematch through manager Virginia St. Ursula, who warned a reporter away from him; One-Winged Angel and the Amity stable celebrated the win on tape. November and T.D. Swagger were billed as potential title challengers afterward. Backstage, Erik and Chad Grimsson clashed with the Privateers over the Drakes' own estranged sister, Lisa; a mystery man bought a single ticket in the Fortress Fraternity section under an assumed name, prompting on-air speculation from the box office staff. Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) and the Fraternity Boys (Chris O'Brien and Brian McKenzie) closed out a night of celebrating their own Gold Rush wins together off-camera.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The posts' own subject line reads "[08.25.04]" but both parts' own opening graphics read "08-28-2004"; 25 August 2004 was a Wednesday, but 28 August 2004 was a Saturday, matching this wing's own established Saturday date for every other Saturday Night Rampage broadcast in the held record, so the graphics' own date is used.

matches.how: Leslie Hernandez beat Lolita Love by pinfall with a cradle after a prolonged assault on Love's own leg.

evidence.note: A friendly rivalry between the co-holders of the Miss Uni title; Niklos Romani accompanied Hernandez, and Lolita raised Hernandez's own arm in victory afterward.

matches.how: Jamie Underwood won the UWF Rampage Championship from Uriah Hawkins by pinfall with a small package after Papa Legba ran in and blindsided Hawkins with the Ragga Bomb.

evidence.note: Legba framed the run-in as payback for Hawkins costing him the Meltdown Championship days earlier; Corporate Leverage handed Underwood a set of brass knuckles that went unused after Hawkins ducked the swing, and "son" Jamie Jr. pulled Hawkins's own hair to distract the referee.

matches.how: Tara Smith beat Tara Marshall by disqualification after Marshall struck her with a tag team title belt in front of the referee. finish: disqualification

evidence.note: Sierra Browne and Dalbello Rage of the Misfits watched from the crowd; Brianna Landis and Marshall continued the beatdown afterward until Alicia Powers ran in to make the save.

matches.how: The Universal Powers won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship from the Sons of Cacaphony in a street fight, an unidentified masked interloper knocking Erik Grimsson out from inside a locker-room closet before Todd Franklin finished him with a superkick for the pin.

evidence.note: The Privateers separately ambushed Chad Grimsson at ringside mid-match, unrelated to either tag team's own title challenge; Niklos and Ravnos Romani ran in to help the Grimssons before the closet ambush turned the finish. The mystery interloper's identity was not revealed.

matches.how: Jason Keening beat Scott "Hotspot" Daniels by pinfall with an inside cradle in his own first UWF singles match.

evidence.note: After the bell, Daniels attacked Keening with a Pridebreaker until a masked man attacked Daniels in turn and then DDT'd Keening, revealing himself as "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas -- the same man who had attacked Michael Keening backstage at Gold Rush -- before Daniels drove Douglas from the ring, telling him this was Daniels's own house, not Keening's.

matches.how: One-Winged Angel retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Michael Bonn, catching a top-rope hurricanrana attempt and turning it into the Revelator for the pin.

evidence.note: Bonn attacked Angel with the title belt after the loss until a thrown water bottle drew him into the crowd, where "Hentai" Ryu Osawa clotheslined him and offered a career-versus-career match; Jessica Marshall approved the match for the following week with conditions attached.

matches.how: The Hands of Death beat Kyle Lee and Alex Kidd in an escape-or-pinfall steel cage main event, Serge Annis and Caliban pinning Kidd with a Near Death Experience superplex-and-slam combination after Lee escaped the cage but could not return in time to help.

evidence.note: Lee climbed a ladder set outside the cage to attack Annis, but Annis took the chair from him before he could use it and Lee fell to the arena floor; both men briefly escaped the cage together early on before the champions dragged them back in.

notes: Opened with World Champion Kyle Lee celebrating his own Gold Rush win before Serge Annis and Caliban confronted him alone in a dark locker room, promising to end his life in that night's own steel cage main event. Leslie Hernandez was assaulted and thrown through a security-office window by the Universal Powers before her own scheduled match, then carried off by the Romani brothers and Tigress for treatment; Alex Kidd was ambushed backstage by Derek Martin, run off by Uriah Hawkins. Donna Tetreault revealed on-air that she had been secretly involved with Brian McKenzie for months, humiliating manager Simon O'Neal in the ring and taking his hat and sunglasses; the Fraternity Boys later found a case of champagne from Jessica Marshall waiting in their own locker room, drained entirely by Chris O'Brien. Victor Frost and new manager Victoria Marquess taunted Quinn Brown, who challenged Frost to a rematch despite their own title match's no-rematch clause. Marissa Monet cut a tirade against Tigress and the Women's Championship's own past holders before the Hands of Death assaulted her ahead of their own main event, Caliban clawing her back open.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 8 September 2004, a Wednesday matching this wing's own established Meltdown weekday.

matches.how: "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas beat Taurus by submission with his own End of the Show cobra clutch in his own UWF debut.

evidence.note: Douglas was seconded by his 450-pound bodyguard, Titanicus. Afterward, Jason Keening walked out to a hero's ovation, snapped his own bowie knife in half in front of Douglas, and left without a word.

matches.how: Paul Wong beat "Dark Horse" Randall Osbourne by pinfall with a lariat off the ropes in the UWF Meltdown Championship tournament's own first round.

evidence.note: Osbourne's manager Cameo interfered twice, including a low blow, before Osbourne accidentally crushed her against the turnbuckles charging in for an avalanche, opening the door for Wong's finish.

matches.how: Vyolynce beat "The First American Badass" Brian McKenzie by pinfall with his own Oblivion chokeslam in the tournament's own first round.

evidence.note: Paul Wong's charge to the ring, still angry over an earlier ambush by McKenzie and Donna Tetreault, distracted McKenzie long enough for the finish.

matches.how: Tigress beat Scorpio by pinfall with the Poacher's Woe after ducking an enzuigiri in the tournament's own first round.

evidence.note: Scorpio was seconded by manager and girlfriend Erika Lima; Tigress advanced to face the winner of Papa Legba and Uriah Hawkins.

matches.how: Papa Legba and Uriah Hawkins fought to a double countout in the tournament's own first round, brawling out of the ring and up the ramp past the referee's ten count.

evidence.note: Manager Holly Williams trailed the brawl to the back; Tigress advanced to the tournament finals on a bye as a result.

matches.how: Team BATTLE*DREAM (Reona Yoshida and Misaki Ishikawa) beat the Bod Squad (Tara "Sunburst" Marshall and Brianna Landis) by disqualification after Marshall drove a chair into Ishikawa's spine to save Landis from a spike piledriver; the UWF Women's Tag Team Championship stayed with the champions under the finish. finish: disqualification

evidence.note: Team BATTLE*DREAM earned the shot with a four corners win the week before; Ishikawa's Hiroshima Starlight and a Reona Entanglement Special EX4 nearly finished the challenge before Marshall's interference.

matches.how: Vyolynce beat Paul Wong by disqualification in the tournament semifinal and advanced to the finals after Brian McKenzie ran in and was caught in Vyolynce's own Embrace of Darkness. finish: disqualification

evidence.note: Donna Tetreault pulled McKenzie from the ring and fled into the crowd with him before Angel could catch either of them.

matches.how: Vyolynce and Tigress wrestled to a twenty-minute time-limit draw in the UWF Meltdown Championship tournament finals, both locked in dueling submissions when the bell sounded.

evidence.note: Jessica "Fatality" Marshall, furious that neither finalist would face champion Collision Holly, announced a three-way submissions match for the Meltdown Championship the following week: Holly versus Tigress versus Vyolynce.

notes: A one-night tournament to crown a challenger for Meltdown Champion Collision Holly, who did not wrestle this show; the finals ended in a draw, so Jessica "Fatality" Marshall booked a three-way submissions match for the title the following week among Holly, Tigress, and Vyolynce. Opened with Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie ambushing an already-injured Simon O'Neal backstage before Paul Wong's own match, and Jason Keening recounting his own history with debuting rival "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas, including an earlier knife attack on Rampage. "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath's own attempt to be released from his contract was refused by Jessica Marshall, who tied his continued employment to his ongoing custody dispute. New signee "The Statewide Sensation" Marcus Nuit gave a nervous, rambling promo previewing his own debut the following week. Tigress visited her injured sister Leslie Hernandez in the hospital, sparred verbally with a reporter and with Angel, and previewed her own intergender opponent, Scorpio.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: Both parts' own subject lines and their own opening graphics agree on 18 September 2004, a Saturday matching this wing's own established Saturday Night Rampage weekday.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship over Brianna Landis by pinfall with the Dominion Day windmill suplex.

evidence.note: Tara "Sunburst" Marshall struck Landis with a tag team title belt to knock her from the top turnbuckle mid-match, then admired her own reflection in the belt while Tetreault finished the cover; Tetreault chose Landis as her challenger after publicly needling both Landis and Marshall.

matches.how: "Violent" Victor Frost beat November by pinfall with a steel chair shot in a non-title match after manager Victoria Marquess revealed mid-match that the bout had been arranged with no disqualifications.

evidence.note: Frost's own UWF North American Heavyweight Championship was not at stake; valets Roxy Mayhem and Simone Sumner interfered against November throughout the match.

matches.how: Caliban and Marissa Monet's "Battle of the Sexes" match was thrown out without a decision after Caliban's tag partner Serge Annis ran in and the two men hit their own Near Death Experience superplex-and-slam combination on Monet.

evidence.note: Monet opened the match hurling a chair at Caliban and had him in trouble for long stretches before he answered with a Reverse Buzzsaw Kick and a Paralyzer press onto the ringpost; Caliban spat on the beaten Monet after Annis's run-in.

matches.how: "Hentai" Ryu Osawa beat Michael Bonn by pinfall with an underhook sit-down powerbomb in a no-disqualification "Career Paths" match, forcing the two into a tag team under the match's own stipulation.

evidence.note: Manager Virginia St. Ursula pulled a steel chair away from Bonn to stop a top-rope Deadfall attempt on Osawa; a furious Bonn accused her of betrayal before Osawa talked him down from attacking her, and Bonn stormed off alone.

matches.how: Ravnos Romani and a substituting Alex Extreme beat Todd Franklin and Jacob Drake by pinfall after Romani blasted Franklin with a pair of brass knuckles and rolled him up.

evidence.note: Erik Grimsson was ruled out by a phony medical hold from Jessica "Fatality" Marshall; Extreme, approved as a last-minute replacement, and Romani opened the match by throwing a handful of the Gypsy Curse powder into Franklin's eyes. A returning Alex Martinez and Michael Augustine's own backstage feud interrupted the match's aftermath.

matches.how: Scott "Hotspot" Daniels and a substituting "Dead End" Derek Martin beat Alex Kidd and Uriah Hawkins by pinfall, Martin's own End chokeslam finishing Kidd although Kidd was not the legal man.

evidence.note: Tom Landis was taken to the hospital after being ambushed backstage with a crowbar by "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas; the referee allowed Martin's late substitution and let the pinfall stand despite Kidd having tagged out moments earlier.

matches.how: Michael Augustine and Alex Martinez's "Singles War" ended without a decision after the Privateers and a returning Alex Extreme turned the brawl into a four-man fight that spilled through the ringside area.

evidence.note: The two men had already fought throughout the arena before the bell; manager Allison Ivey struck Martinez with a high kick during the match itself.

matches.how: Kyle Lee retained the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World over Jamie Underwood by disqualification after owner Edmond Winston IV struck him with a steel chair; the title does not change hands on a disqualification. finish: disqualification

evidence.note: Winston went on to superplex Lee from the top rope through a steel ladder propped against the ring apron and knocked out Tesla St. James with a pair of knuckledusters after she tried to fight him off.

notes: Opened with Alex Martinez vowing revenge on Michael Augustine over a racial slur from Meltdown, and the debuting Sons of Cacaphony's own scrambled-tag partner Ravnos Romani being left without Erik Grimsson after a phony medical exclusion by Jessica "Fatality" Marshall; One-Winged Angel and the Amity stable challenged Augustine's own street credibility on camera. The Universal Powers, newly-crowned North American Tag Team Champions, taunted the Privateers in a shared locker room over the Youngbloods' own recent conduct. "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson addressed the Love Sisters' own criticism of her ongoing feud with Leanna Love in a lengthy interview. Tom Landis was hospitalized backstage in a crowbar attack by "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas, forcing Derek Martin's late substitution into the tag match against Alex Kidd and Uriah Hawkins.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 22 September 2004, a Wednesday matching this wing's own established Meltdown weekday.

matches.how: "The Statewide Sensation" Marcus Nuit beat Job Holly by pinfall with a rolling savate kick into a running Lyger Bomb in his own in-ring UWF debut.

evidence.note: A quick, clean debut win built around speed: a running elbowsmash, a legwhip takedown, a high armdrag to the floor, and a springboard fistdrop before the finish. Nuit celebrated at length with the fans afterward.

matches.how: The Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) and Alex Martinez beat the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) and Randall Osbourne by pinfall, Martinez and Erik Grimsson combining on Todd Franklin with a version of the Harlequins' own Reality Check.

evidence.note: Managers Cameo and Rodney both worked ringside for Osbourne and Martinez respectively. The match followed a backstage vignette in which Martinez tested the Grimsson brothers in a gym workout before agreeing to team with them.

matches.how: Dalbello Rage beat Lolita Love by pinfall with a super cradleplex after grinding down Love's legs for much of the match.

evidence.note: Love had prepared with scouting tape from her cousin Lara Leigh Love, a wrestler who had beaten Rage repeatedly in a rival promotion; Rage suplexed Love over the top rope into sister Leanna's arms after the bell and complained she deserved better competition than Meltdown offers.

matches.how: Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith beat Extreme Measures (Nina Grimsson, Lisa Drake) by pinfall, Smith's top-rope Arizona Rattler finishing Drake after Powers's own Michinoku Driver.

evidence.note: A clean contest with a handshake on both ends; Powers absorbed a German suplex and a top-rope frog splash from Drake before turning the match with an enzuigiri.

matches.how: The One-Winged Angel retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over "The Drunken Icon" Chris O'Brien by pinfall with the Heavenly Wind and Hell's Halo combination, dubbed "Divine Intervention" by cornerwoman Ami Tran.

evidence.note: A friendly, hard-fought contest between former MBC rivals turned friends; both men embraced after the bell and left together with Amity.

matches.how: Tigress won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Collision Holly by submission with the Marjara Mallaka, sitting her full weight across Holly's legs until he tapped.

evidence.note: Billed as a three-way submissions match against both Tigress and Vyolynce, but Vyolynce cut a promo declaring himself "nobody's pawn," refused to participate, and left the ring before the bell, leaving Tigress to face Holly alone.

notes: Opened with a backstage vignette in which Alex Martinez tested the Grimsson brothers in a gym workout, ending in a three-way handshake ahead of their own six-man tag. A pre-match video introduced Marcus Nuit's own nervous debut promo from the week before. The advertised Team Canada-versus-Fury tag match never began: Team Canada ambushed Fury (Rage, Spice) during their own entrance, Tom Landis crutch-attacked One-Winged Angel, and the brawl spilled out until Amity ran off the Pride, the referee waving the contest off without a bell. "The Drunken Icon" Chris O'Brien's own drunken, censored monologue previewed his Cruiserweight title challenge. T.D. Swagger staged an elaborate stunt on Quinn Brown and Uriah Hawkins, hanging himself from the rafters over a mocked-up hotel eviction to needle them into confronting owner Edmond Winston IV's own treatment of the roster; both men shook his hand and agreed to meet him afterward. Tigress visited the shrine of her late friend Ogre with her sister Leslie Hernandez, previewing the Meltdown Championship match; the finish saw Vyolynce declare himself "nobody's pawn" and depart, leaving Tigress to beat Collision Holly alone. The broadcast closed with "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas taunting Jason Keening ahead of the following week's guest-refereed match, and Scott "Hotspot" Daniels vowing revenge on Douglas after the crowbar attack on Tom Landis.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: Both parts' own subject lines and their own opening graphics agree on 2 October 2004, a Saturday matching this wing's own established Saturday Night Rampage weekday.

matches.how: "The Savior" Jamie Underwood retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "Mr. Excitement" Alex Extreme by pinfall with his own Signed, Sealed, and Delivered split-legged moonsault.

evidence.note: Underwood's bodyguard Corporate Leverage and "son" Jamie Jr. worked the ringside area throughout; a returning Privateers (Edward and Jacob Drake) turned a near-finish into a five-on-one beatdown of Extreme after a chair shot from Jacob Drake, before Underwood hit his finisher for the pin.

matches.how: Sabbath won a non-title three-way dance over Papa Legba and Quinn Brown with the Black Zero reverse hurricanrana, pinning Legba.

evidence.note: Jessica "Fatality" Marshall came to ringside mid-match to berate Sabbath for "dogging it," needling him over his ongoing custody dispute; the taunt visibly spurred Sabbath into the rally that won the match. Brown and Sabbath shook hands afterward.
