matches.how: "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas and Scott "Hotspot" Daniels fought to a double disqualification under special guest referee Jason Keening.

evidence.note: Keening banned Douglas's bodyguard Titanicus from ringside and pulled a chair away from Daniels mid-match; caught between the fighters' fists trying to break up a double stranglehold, Keening called for the bell, tore off his referee's shirt, and clotheslined both men from the ring.

matches.how: "The Show" Sierra Browne and Team BATTLE*DREAM (Reona Yoshida, Misaki Ishikawa) beat Donna Tetreault and the Bod Squad (Tara "Sunburst" Marshall, Brianna Landis) by pinfall, Sierra Browne finishing Landis with the Truth Superkick.

evidence.note: Not a title match. Tetreault was missing at the bell and the Bod Squad started the match a woman short before Tetreault surfaced late, disguised in a blonde wig among the Greece fan section; Misaki Ishikawa tasered Tara "Sunburst" Marshall mid-match. Tetreault ambushed Sierra Browne with a title-belt shot to the shoulder after the bell and left with the Women's Heavyweight title still around her waist.

matches.how: Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) beat the Hands of Death (Serge Annis, Caliban) by pinfall, Sebastian pinning Annis (grabbing a handful of tights for leverage) after Tucker tripped Annis off a superplex attempt.

evidence.note: Tucker distracted Caliban with a thrown frozen fish moments before the finish. After the bell, the returning Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) attacked both Hands of Death members with their own tag title belts, having earlier in the show saved Marissa Monet from a beatdown by the same pairing.

matches.how: Uriah Hawkins beat "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall with an Oklahoma side roll in the main event, capitalizing when Martin's own worked-over knee buckled mid-charge.

evidence.note: Hawkins had cut a pre-match promo on respect in professional wrestling, naming Martin directly. After the bell, Scott "Hotspot" Daniels and the Pride (Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski, Kari Stevens, Tom Landis) interrupted, offering Martin a spot in the Pride in place of the injured Landis; Martin took the microphone, dropped it without a word, and walked past Daniels and out of the arena.

notes: Opened with Marissa Monet addressing her own recent beating by the Hands of Death, only for Serge Annis and Caliban to attack her again; a returning Shadoe Rage, half of the once-champion Prophets of Rage, made the save before his own tag partner Derek Rage arrived with a chair to fend off both attackers, the four brawling to a standoff. Backstage, Quinn Brown promised to make Victor Frost pay for his own recent conduct as manager Victoria Marquess spoke for an absent, dismissive Frost ahead of the triple threat. After Underwood's win, Michael Augustine ambushed Alex Extreme's manager Rodney at the loading dock, beating him with a steel chair and hurling him head-first into a garage door in revenge for Extreme costing him the UWF World Heavyweight Championship; Extreme found Rodney only after the assault and left for the hospital. Jessica "Fatality" Marshall staged a fake return of a Portland-associated promoter before Becky Byers cut her off, the two women booking next week's Miami card: an eight-man tag captained by Edmond Winston IV and Alex Extreme, with the fourth man on Winston's side kept secret by Marshall, and a mystery challenger for Jamie Underwood's own Rampage Championship kept secret by Byers. Sabbath's wife Sayaka worried aloud over their ongoing custody fight in a hotel-room phone call with their daughter before Sabbath himself arrived, second-guessing his own fitness as a father. The main event closed the show with Scott "Hotspot" Daniels's on-air recruitment pitch to Derek Martin, invoking the unmasked UWF legend Humanity as a cautionary tale; Martin turned the offer down in silence.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 6 October 2004, a Wednesday matching this wing's own established Meltdown weekday.

matches.how: Taurus beat Simon O'Neal by pinfall after Simon collapsed under his own weight attempting a bodyslam, an upset that stunned the crowd into silence.

evidence.note: O'Neal looked visibly disinterested coming to the ring; a thumb to the eye briefly turned the tide before the botched slam decided it. O'Neal walked to the back without protest.

matches.how: "The Statewide Sensation" Marcus Nuit beat Steve Ryott by pinfall, rolling the returning cruiserweight up in a surprise inside cradle.

evidence.note: A back-and-forth technical bout; Ryott favored his own recently-injured ankle throughout but still worked in a top-rope diving splash before the finish. Nuit celebrated wildly, extending Ryott's own handshake courtesy afterward but not noticing it.

matches.how: "Dead End" Derek Martin beat Vyolynce by pinfall with a hanging brainbuster suplex.

evidence.note: A hard-hitting brawl that spilled to the floor before the bell; Vyolynce countered the Dead End with a standing neck vice, the first time the finisher had been reversed in the held record, before Martin's own counter ended it.

matches.how: Fury (Rage and Spice) and Ami Tran beat Team Canada (Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski) and Kari Stevens by pinfall, Tran finishing Stevens with a version of the One-Winged Angel's own Revelator.

evidence.note: Ami Tran's own first competitive UWF match, cornering for Fury and the One-Winged Angel in prior broadcasts; Spice set up the finish by benchpressing Stevens across Tran's outstretched knee. A masked interloper, "1WA," was seconding Amity from ringside throughout and praised Tran's showing afterward.

matches.how: The Privateers retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship over Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) by pinfall, Edward Drake pinning Sebastian off a DDT while Jacob Drake illegally held Tucker's own feet to keep him from breaking up the cover.

evidence.note: Both teams attacked before the bell; Tucker isolated and battered the champions for several minutes before a tornado DDT let Sebastian back in, only for the Privateers' own cheating finish to steal the match.

matches.how: Tigress retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Youth Gone Wild by submission with an inverted dragon sleeper.

evidence.note: A competitive title defense with several near-falls in both directions; Youth Gone Wild extended a handshake afterward, which Tigress accepted to a large ovation.

notes: Opened with a locker-room scene in which Jamie Underwood's own "son" Alex slipped away to visit Tigress's pet tiger Harley unsupervised, drawing Tigress's own fury at Underwood once she found the boy safe; Sabbath needled Underwood backstage afterward over the strain of unwanted fatherhood. Jessica "Fatality" Marshall and returning "Superstar" Stephanie Harper traded barbs over the promotion's own state under Marshall Law. Donna Tetreault taunted a increasingly hollowed-out Simon O'Neal, who later told Rampage announcer Amy Marshall he was considering retirement. Backstage in the empty Portland arena after the previous Rampage, Serge Annis and Caliban vowed revenge on the returning Prophets of Rage over an earlier frozen-fish incident, Annis fixating on a taunt from Shadoe Rage. The Amity faction (Fury, Ami Tran, and the One-Winged Angel) cut a promo on their own ongoing feud with the Pride. Michael Bonn, "Hentai" Ryu Osawa, and manager Virginia St. Ursula previewed the pair's own first tag match together, against the Sons of Cacaphony, with Bonn visibly resentful of the forced partnership. Jason Keening's uncle, retired grappler Ken Keening, visited backstage and urged his nephew to keep a level head against Chris Douglas and Scott Daniels. The Privateers dismissed Strictly Business's own recent wins in an interview before their own title defense. The broadcast closed with Quinn Brown delivering a lengthy challenge to Edmond Winston IV and Victor Frost, naming Uriah Hawkins, Alex Extreme, and Alex Martinez as allies and inviting Papa Legba to bring on the fight.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 16 October 2004, a Saturday matching this wing's own established Saturday Night Rampage weekday.

matches.how: Scott "Hotspot" Daniels won a three-way dance over "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas and Jason Keening, stealing a pinfall on Keening after Keening and Douglas collided head-first and both went down.

evidence.note: Douglas's own bodyguard Titanicus was pepper-sprayed away from ringside by Keening's manager Kari Stevens' own kick backfiring on her; Daniels barely avoided the finish himself after being launched over the top rope to the floor earlier in the match.

matches.how: "Showtime" Rick Marley won the UWF Rampage Championship from Jamie Underwood by pinfall with a small package, catching the champion off guard after Underwood turned his back on the match to check on his own distracted "son."

evidence.note: Special guest referee T.D. Swagger ejected Underwood's own bodyguard Corporate Leverage from ringside mid-match for interference. Underwood's own outburst at the boy afterward, blaming him for the loss, drew a returning Sabbath's own assault before Sabbath recognized the child as his own son and the two reconciled in the ring; Underwood then revealed on camera that his entire guardianship of the boy had been a deliberate, months-long scheme to torment Sabbath.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over "Battle Princess" Misaki Ishikawa by disqualification after Ishikawa was found with a taser at ringside.

evidence.note: Ishikawa had Tetreault beaten clean with the Skull Crash Buster before Brian McKenzie pulled her out of the cover; the taser, planted by McKenzie's own side, never actually worked when Ishikawa tried to use it on Tetreault afterward. Tetreault finished her with a Minnie Driver post-match before leaving with the belt.

matches.how: "Hentai" Ryu Osawa and "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn, forced into a tag team by the terms of Osawa's own prior win over Bonn, beat the Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) by disqualification when Erik Grimsson attacked a non-competing Jacob Drake at ringside.

evidence.note: The pairing's own first match together; Bonn and Osawa showed genuine, if strained, teamwork before the finish. The Privateers had come to ringside uninvited to scout the match, and Erik Grimsson's retaliation for their own earlier parking-lot ambush of Alex Extreme's manager Rodney drew the referee's decision. The finish set off a building-wide brawl that consumed the remainder of the broadcast (see below).

notes: Opened at a Miami hospital, where Alex Martinez, Erik and Chad Grimsson kept vigil over the hospitalized Rodney (manager to Alex Extreme's own persona) with a visiting associate of Rodney's own substance-abuse recovery program, worried Extreme's own sobriety was now at risk. In the arena parking lot the Grimssons and Martinez ambushed the Youngbloods (Michael Augustine, Jacob and Edward Drake, Allison Ivey) in retaliation for the beating that hospitalized Rodney; Extreme himself then beat a bloodied Augustine with a baseball bat until Martinez physically stopped him from going further. A taped promo had Chris Douglas mock special guest referee Jason Keening ahead of the night's own three-way dance. In a comic backstage interlude, Chris O'Brien, Brian McKenzie, and Donna Tetreault played basketball while Keith "Hellsing" Marshall returned from a supply run; Misaki Ishikawa cut a promo vowing to take the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship for herself. After the Sons of Cacaphony/Osawa-Bonn finish, an unprecedented building-wide riot broke out and consumed the rest of the broadcast: the Privateers and Sons of Cacaphony brawled into the crowd, Amity and the Pride collided, Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme's own allies fought the Youngbloods across the arena floor, and the fighting spread backstage through nearly every locker room and hallway in the building. Alicia Powers was buried under a row of tipped-over lockers by the Bod Squad; commissioner Becky Byers was speared through a temporary office wall by Serge Annis, colliding with new champion Rick Marley in the middle of contract talks; announcer David Rogers left the broadcast position to try to break up the fighting and was knocked unconscious by a stray chair shot. The chaos ultimately reached the production truck, where Michael Augustine and Erik Grimsson's own fight on top of the cab knocked the broadcast off the air entirely; the previously advertised eight-man main event (Alex Extreme, Quinn Brown, Alex Martinez, and Uriah Hawkins against Edmond Winston IV, Victor Frost, Papa Legba, and an unnamed fourth partner) never took place. A follow-up special program the next day recapped the aftermath and the roster's own injuries (collected, not served, as it records no reign or roster change).

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 20 October 2004, a Wednesday matching this wing's own established Meltdown weekday.

matches.how: Brick Rosen beat Zero-G by submission (a Boston crab) in a UWF tryout match.

evidence.note: Zero-G, a local South Florida high flyer, dazzled the crowd with a springboard armdrag and a triple jump moonsault before Rosen countered a guardrail-running huracanrana with a powerbomb that turned the tide; a gutwrench powerbomb and a Boston crab finished it.

matches.how: "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb beat Taurus by pinfall with the Atom Smasher, a double underhook piledriver, in his own UWF debut.

evidence.note: Malcomb brawled power-against-power with Taurus, who was coming off his own upset win over Simon O'Neal the previous Meltdown; a scoop powerslam nearly turned the tide for Taurus before Malcomb's own finisher ended it.

matches.how: "The Bayou Badboy" Colby Greene retained the UWF Eurasian Heavyweight Championship over "The Hero" Marcus Johnson by pinfall (the Bayou Bomb, a sitdown Last Ride-type powerbomb).

evidence.note: Both wrestlers are billed from the UWF-Eurasia roster, making their first appearance on the flagship Meltdown card; Greene, wrestling in his own hometown of Baton Rouge, was cheered early but turned the crowd against him by tearing up a fan's sign naming his uncle, Brett Greene.

matches.how: "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson beat Leanna Love by pinfall (the Dragon Spike) in a lumberjill match, with the rest of the women's division surrounding the ring.

evidence.note: The match settled a friendship-turned-rivalry running nearly two years; Brianna Landis and Kari Stevens assaulted Love when she was thrown from the ring, until Lisa Drake made the save for her, then herself beat down Love for Sonya Benedict before Love's own sister Lolita broke it up. Grimsson finished Love with the Dragon Spike after Love reversed a Marine Throat Lock into a Samoan drop.

matches.how: "Tornado" Tara Smith and Reona Yoshida were both declared the winner of a women's three-way dance over Brianna Landis after each locked on a separate submission hold on the unconscious Landis at the same moment, the referee awarding each of them a future UWF Women's Tag Team Championship match against the Bod Squad.

evidence.note: Landis knocked herself out attempting a top-rope tornado DDT on Smith, who ducked clear; Yoshida then locked on a double armbar and Smith a Boston crab on the unconscious Landis simultaneously, leaving the referee to call a shared win rather than rule a single victor.

matches.how: Derek Rage beat Caliban by pinfall (the Hammer of God) after an ally, Pizzazz, jabbed a lit cigarette into Caliban's eye at ringside during a brawl between tag partner Shadoe Rage and Serge Annis.

evidence.note: Rage nearly lost the match to a reversed Paralyzer and a low blow before the interference turned it; the Prophets of Rage left ringside smirking as Serge Annis rolled into the ring to check on a wounded Caliban.

matches.how: Tigress retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Bobby Nash by pinfall (the Sumatran Headhunter), using the ropes for leverage on the cover.

evidence.note: Nash, a UWF-Eurasia wrestler billed at seven feet tall, mocked the champion's size before the bell; Tigress worked his legs throughout, weakening him enough to close the size gap for the finish.

matches.how: The Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos Romani) won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship from the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) by pinfall, Niklos pinning Lincoln with a neckbreaker delivered off his own brother's shoulders.

evidence.note: A returning Vyolynce appeared at ringside with a chair partway through the match, distracting the champions; the Romanis, previously billed together in this wing as the Arcana, framed the win as payback for an earlier assault on their own cornerwoman, Leslie Hernandez.

notes: Opened with Caliban delivering a message to owner Edmond Winston IV on behalf of the Hands of Death, ending their own working arrangement with him over an unpaid debt, then beating him down alongside Serge Annis. Amity (One-Winged Angel, Ami Tran, Rage, Spice) announced a coming push against the New Era's own leadership, naming Jessica Marshall, Edmond Winston IV, and Jamie Underwood directly. Backstage, Chad Grimsson recovered in hospital from the previous Rampage's own riot with sister Nina, girlfriend Sonya Benedict, and a visiting Sabbath, who thanked the Grimssons for helping him against Jamie Underwood; T.D. Swagger, working as a referee, cut a promo defending Dave Rogers and vowing to keep working both in the ring and in the stripes. Alicia Powers recovered in hospital as well, her husband Alex Kidd overhearing Tara Marshall complain about the medical attention Powers was receiving before the two clashed; Tom Landis needled Kidd about recent losses. "Hentai" Ryu Osawa reported on a hospitalized Virginia St. Ursula's own condition, worried that tag partner Michael Bonn had not visited; the Love Sisters discussed the toll of the Miami riot ahead of Leanna's own match. "Tornado" Tara Smith cut a promo previewing her own three-way dance. The returning Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) confronted Moe Owens backstage, Derek warning the Hands of Death ahead of Shadoe's own upcoming match with Serge Annis. The broadcast closed with the debuting Zero-G's own opponent Brick Rosen name-dropped again backstage and two further hospital-set vignettes recapping the Miami brawl's injuries.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 30 October 2004, a Saturday matching this wing's own established Saturday Night Rampage weekday.

matches.how: "Showtime" Rick Marley retained the UWF Rampage Championship over Brian McKenzie by countout, after McKenzie abandoned the match to save tag partner Chris O'Brien from a beating.

evidence.note: McKenzie had Marley reeling with a DDT and was setting up his own Minnie Driver finisher when he spotted, on the arena screen, Michael Bonn dropping O'Brien onto the loading dock concrete; McKenzie broke off the match and ran to help, forfeiting by countout with the finish in reach.

matches.how: Shadoe Rage won by forfeit when Serge Annis vanished from the entrance ramp during an extended standoff and never appeared for the bell.

evidence.note: Annis struck his own crucifix pose at the top of the aisle through several minutes of lighting and music cues, then disappeared entirely when the arena lights returned; the Prophets of Rage's own locker room was set ablaze afterward by a delivered shipment of frozen fish, an apparent fan retaliation for an earlier parking-lot incident.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over Kari Stevens by submission (a crossface, rubbing salt and lemon juice into a cut over Stevens's own eye).

evidence.note: The referee confiscated salt from Stevens and brass knuckles from Tetreault before the bell; Trevor Hextall later threw salt meant for Tetreault that blinded her instead, but Tetreault had brought her own water and a salted lemon wedge, using the wedge to finish Stevens once a cut opened above her eye.

matches.how: Jamie Underwood and "Dead End" Derek Martin beat Alex Kidd and Sabbath by pinfall, Underwood countering Sabbath's own Coffin Breaker II attempt into a sitting pin.

evidence.note: Special guest referee T.D. Swagger enforced the match closely; after the bell Underwood and Martin armed themselves with steel chairs and beat down both fallen opponents and Sabbath's wife Sayaka before the referee could intervene.

matches.how: The One-Winged Angel beat "Agony" Michael Augustine by disqualification after Erik Grimsson pulled Augustine off the top rope to stop a chair-assisted diving attack.

evidence.note: Both men ignored the referee for long stretches of a brutal brawl; once Grimsson's save drew the disqualification, the Privateers and manager Allison Ivey joined the fight, and Scott Daniels left the announce table to help beat down Angel, busting him open.

matches.how: The team of Edmond Winston IV, Victor Frost, Papa Legba, and Luke Kinsey won a Tower of Doom cage match over Quinn Brown, Uriah Hawkins, Alex Extreme, and Alex Martinez when all four members of Winston's own team escaped the tower structure first, Winston last of all after Alex Martinez threw him bodily out of the top cage's own door.

evidence.note: Frost, Legba, and Kinsey each escaped the three-tier cage in turn over the course of the match, leaving Winston trapped alone with Extreme after Martinez, Brown, and Hawkins had all also escaped; a surprise-returning "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee, disguised as a cameraman, attacked Winston to stop him simply walking out unopposed, and Brown freed a trapped Extreme by working the cage switch. All four of Winston's opponents then beat him down inside the cage with his own solid gold knuckles until Martinez threw him overhead and out through the cage door; the impact and the fall left him unconscious and bleeding as the referee, having recovered from an earlier collision, called for the bell on seeing him outside the structure.

notes: Opened with Jessica Marshall announcing a bounty on ten wrestlers she blamed for the Miami riot (Alex Kidd, Chris O'Brien, Erik Grimsson, Sabbath, Jason Keening, the One-Winged Angel, Quinn Brown, and Alex Martinez named twice) before revealing her own mystery Tower of Doom partner, debuting star Luke Kinsey. Michael Bonn viciously assaulted Chris O'Brien backstage during the opening title match, smashing his own laptop over him and slamming him against a wall; Alex Extreme separately beat down a Jessica Marshall aide with a baseball bat, demanding a match with Michael Augustine. Alex Kidd confronted a locked office door demanding to see Edmond Winston IV, taunted by Jamie Underwood about his hospitalized wife before storming off to prepare for the tag match. Donna Tetreault ambushed Stephanie Harper backstage with her own title belt in revenge for the Miami brawl; Sierra Browne intervened, accidentally striking an already-fallen Harper with a superkicked chair meant for Tetreault, and was thrown out of the building by Jessica Marshall's own security before carrying Harper to the trainers herself. "Screaming Drillbit" Jason Keening was struck unconscious backstage with a chair by "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas ahead of the main event. Victor Frost cut a promo naming his own eight-man main event opponents before an argument with his girlfriend, Vicky, interrupted him. The show closed with Quinn Brown embracing a returning "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee, welcoming him back to the UWF as the crowd celebrated the reversal of the Tower of Doom's own finish.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 3 November 2004, a Wednesday matching this wing's own established Meltdown weekday.

matches.how: Vyolynce beat "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb by pinfall (Oblivion, a sacrifice-the-knee driver).

evidence.note: Malcomb, coming off his own UWF debut win the prior show, took control early with a cradle neckbreaker and a knee-focused ground attack; Vyolynce, hobbling on the same knee he sacrificed twice for a Shining Wizard variant and Oblivion, finished the newcomer off, leaving him slow to recover from the concussion-inducing move.

matches.how: Dalbello Rage beat Angel by pinfall (a cradle-plex).

evidence.note: Egged on ringside by Sierra Browne, Rage countered a near-fall German suplex attempt from Angel and finished with the cradle-plex, Sierra instructing the cameraman to get "the money shot" of the cover.

matches.how: The Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) beat Collision Holly and Job Holly by pinfall.

evidence.note: Shadoe blinded Collision Holly with his own cape for an opening lariat before either Holly could get set; the Prophets combined for the Apocalypse on Job Holly for the finish, then issued a further warning to the Hands of Death on the way out.

matches.how: Luke Kinsey beat "Dark Horse" Randall Osbourne by pinfall (the Lowlife Driver, an inverted DDT) in his own first singles match for the wing.

evidence.note: Kinsey mocked Osbourne as washed up beforehand; Osbourne nearly turned the size difference into a win, heaving Kinsey over the top rope, before a springboard moonsault escape and a turnbuckle-assisted inverted DDT finished it. Osbourne was seconded at ringside by manager Cameo.

matches.how: Tigress retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn by disqualification, after a six-wrestler UWF tryout group ran in to attack Bonn.

evidence.note: Bonn had turned the match around with a turnbuckle powerbomb and a dragon sleeper before an elderly ringside fan revealed himself as T.D. Swagger in disguise, dancing an enzuiguri into Bonn before Zero-G, Brick Rosen, "Gunman" Danny Cole, Wendy Minow, Overkill and Hellhound stormed the ring and beat Bonn down, drawing the disqualification; Swagger framed the group as UWF tryout talent auditioning to "make their names count."

matches.how: "Agony" Michael Augustine and Scott "Hotspot" Daniels fought to a no-contest after Kari Stevens and Allison Ivey each struck the opposing man with a chair and Amity ran in on both wrestlers.

evidence.note: The two brawled through the ring and to the floor, introducing chairs after the referee was knocked down; once Stevens and Ivey had both struck the other man's wrestler, the official called for the bell, only for Amity (the One-Winged Angel, Spice, Rage) to charge the ring and beat down both Augustine and Daniels along with Tom Landis, Ivey and Stevens to a chant of "Amity".

notes: Marcus Nuit, filling in as "Master of Meltdown" while recovering from his own Miami concussion, talked his way past Jessica Marshall by phone into hosting again. Vyolynce and his sister Angel discussed the still-unsolved mystery of who helped the Universal Powers win their tag titles in Indianapolis, Vyolynce warning that "the hunt" was beginning against Malcomb and the Rages. "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb was shown backstage tormenting an unnamed local heckler. Sabbath talked his own father, cardiologist William Price, into a kneebrace prescription so he could keep pursuing Jamie Underwood over an attack on Sabbath's wife Sayaka, with mother Diana and the family's children looking on. "Violent" Victor Frost reconciled with manager Victoria Marquess over failing to protect her during the Miami riot, vowing to punish Uriah Hawkins in his own upcoming Rampage title defense. Derek Martin visited a newly-released Alicia Powers in the hospital to threaten husband Alex Kidd, who vowed renewed focus on Martin now that Kyle Lee had returned. Papa Legba invited Alex Extreme to a New Orleans cafe to apologize for his own past as muscle for a Mississippi crime boss and for following Edmond Winston IV's orders in the Tower of Doom cage, offering a truce Extreme angrily refused. UWF reporter Peter Phillips relayed that the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) were attacked and injured by the same mystery trio that had helped them win the UWF North American Tag Team Championship months earlier, its leader vowing on tape that "the days of reckoning" for the UWF were coming. The returning Prophets of Rage, with Marissa Monet and Pizzazz, targeted the Hands of Death (Serge Annis, Caliban) over the Universal Powers attack ahead of a Rampage tag match against Team Canada. "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson called Jessica Marshall to announce she was ending her own feud with Leanna Love. Tigress visited sister Leslie Hernandez, handcuffed by the traveling Romanis for her own safety, ahead of the Meltdown Championship defense. Jason Keening, in a taped promo, vowed to settle a seven-year grudge with Chris Douglas by first going through bodyguard Titanicus on Rampage.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 13 November 2004, a Saturday matching this wing's own established Saturday Night Rampage weekday.

matches.how: Jamie Underwood beat Papa Legba by disqualification, after Sabbath ran in with a nightstick and struck Legba.

evidence.note: Legba was working over Underwood's knee and had him reeling when Sabbath vaulted the guardrail and blindsided Legba with a nightstick, drawing the disqualification; Underwood then turned the weapon on Sabbath until a wave of fan favorites (Uriah Hawkins, Erik Grimsson, Scorpio, Steve Ryott, Alex Extreme, Alex Kidd and Fury) ran in and chased Underwood from the ring.

matches.how: "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas and "Dead End" Derek Martin fought to a no-contest after Alex Kidd struck Martin from behind.

evidence.note: Martin had Douglas reeling with a hangman's neckbreaker when the arrival of Jason Keening and Alex Kidd distracted him; Douglas whipped Martin into both men, and Kidd struck Martin, drawing the disqualification call before the match degenerated into a four-man brawl that also pulled in the Sons of Cacaphony, Chris O'Brien and the One-Winged Angel.

matches.how: The Hands of Death (Caliban, Serge Annis) and Team Canada (Bob Jablonski, Trevor Hextall) fought to a no-contest.

evidence.note: Hextall broke a hockey stick across Caliban's knee and Kari Stevens tried to slip Trevor a hidden hockey stick of her own, but a member of Fury (Spice) hitting on Stevens at ringside sparked a wider brawl that drew in the Sons of Cacaphony, Uriah Hawkins, Alex Martinez and Alex Extreme before the referee declared the match a no contest.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault's defense of the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World against "Alluring" Arielle Starr ended without a finish after a wave of fan favorites ran in.

evidence.note: Tetreault had loaded a chain into her glove when Sierra Browne, Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith ran to ringside; a chain-loaded shot aimed at Tetreault instead struck Brian McKenzie, who had thrown himself in front of her, and the champion fled to the back with the title still around her waist as the Bod Squad (Tara Marshall, Brianna Landis) were themselves run off by the same group of fan favorites.

matches.how: The Privateers' impromptu UWF World Tag Team Championship defense against Alex Martinez and "Mr. Excitement" Alex Extreme ended in a no contest after "Agony" Michael Augustine ran in and broke a Singapore cane over Extreme's head.

evidence.note: Martinez and Extreme had dominated much of the match, Martinez hitting his own Firebomb on Jacob Drake, before Augustine's interference busted Extreme open; the Sons of Cacaphony, Steve Ryott and the One-Winged Angel ran in and cleared the ring of both the Privateers and Augustine, the referee having already called for the bell.

matches.how: "Violent" Victor Frost retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over Quinn Brown by pinfall (a high-elevation Death Valley Driver).

evidence.note: Brown appeared to have the match won after a missile dropkick, but Frost pulled his own manager Simone Sumner into the dropkick's path to save himself, leaving her unconscious; Brown paused to check on her before Frost finished him with the Death Valley Driver off the second rope. Brown carried the injured Sumner to the back afterward.

matches.how: Edmond Winston IV beat Alex Kidd in the main event, a Tuxedo Death Match, when Kidd failed to answer referee Ingraham's ten count after a cobra clutch suplex.

evidence.note: The brawl used a trash can, a broom, a coil of wire, brass knuckles, an exposed concrete floor and Winston's own limousine, including a DDT through the vehicle's windshield by Kidd; Winston survived an eight count and a low blow with an Xbox before finishing Kidd with a Black Tie Suplex. A returning Scott Daniels and Team Canada dragged the bloodied Winston to safety in his limousine before Kyle Lee, Alex Martinez and Paul Wong could reach him.

notes: UWF Commissioner Becky Byers, recovering from Serge Annis's own Miami spear, arrived in the Fratmobile with Brian McKenzie and Chris O'Brien to rally the promotion's fan favorites in the parking lot against Marshall Law. Jason Keening confronted "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas and bodyguard Titanicus backstage ahead of Douglas's own match. Sabbath challenged Jamie Underwood to a Last Man Standing match at the promotion's own next pay-per-view. Luke Kinsey needled, then won over, Scott "Hotspot" Daniels backstage by claiming credit for ending Chris Courtade's career. The Hands of Death cut a promo daring the returning Prophets of Rage to name their own stipulation for a future match. Luke Kinsey also needled Jamie Underwood over his own stalled push, offering to broker a bodyguard detail and Knicks tickets; Underwood accepted the tickets but turned down the offer. "Hentai" Ryu Osawa confronted his own forced tag partner "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn over a secret meeting with Jessica Marshall and was shoved into a wall for his trouble. Quinn Brown cut a rallying promo naming the UWF's own five rebelling fan favorites (himself, Kyle Lee, Uriah Hawkins, Alex Extreme, Alex Martinez) before the promotion's fan-favorite roster filled the ring to confront Edmond Winston IV and Jessica Marshall directly; UWF employee Job Holly produced the promotion's own rulebook to show that Winston, as an owner, had never been eligible to challenge for the World Heavyweight Championship at Gold Rush. Under pressure, Winston staked 45 percent of his own UWF ownership across nine pay-per-view matches (five percent a match) between his and Marshall's own side and Byers's, headlined by a Ladder match putting the World Heavyweight Championship and shares on the line between champion Kyle Lee and Winston himself; further matches named for the card included Alex Kidd against Derek Martin and Jamie Underwood against Sabbath, alongside a Sierra Browne-Stephanie Harper match the following week to decide Donna Tetreault's own next Women's Heavyweight Championship challenger and a tag match pitting the One-Winged Angel and Fury against Scott Daniels and Team Canada. Longtime commentator Dave Rogers returned to the broadcast booth to a standing ovation following his own Miami injuries.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 17 November 2004, a Wednesday matching this wing's own established Meltdown weekday.

matches.how: L. Dan Dee beat Zero-G in his own UWF debut when the referee stopped the match after Zero-G passed out in the Figura-Cuatro Leglock.

evidence.note: Both men traded high-risk offense, including a pescado dive to the floor and a flying legdrop, before Dan Dee blocked a Gravitron attempt with a raised knee and locked on the leglock for the finish, managed to the ring by Olivia Michaels.

matches.how: "Smooth as Silk" Miguel Quesada beat "Gunman" Danny Cole by pinfall (a shooting star press) in his own UWF debut.

evidence.note: Cole knocked Quesada to the floor with a backdrop and traded the advantage for several minutes before Quesada's own agility, including a jumping double knee and a springboard corkscrew legdrop, set up the shooting star press for the win; Quesada was accompanied by valet Talia DiMartino and bodyguard Swoll.

matches.how: "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb beat debuting "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by pinfall (the Atom Splitter).

evidence.note: Both big men slugged it out evenly until Embrey, setting up his own powerbomb, paused at the top of the move and allowed Malcomb to counter with a throat shot and the Atom Splitter; Embrey was accompanied by valet Farmer Johnson's Daughter.

matches.how: Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) and the Sons of Cacaphony (Chad and Erik Grimsson) fought to a no-contest.

evidence.note: A technically sharp, well-received match was in progress, with Erik Grimsson building to a possible win off a skytwister press, when the Privateers rushed the ring and hit Erik with the High-Seas Shipwreck, prompting the referee to call for the bell.

matches.how: The Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos Romani) retained the UWF North American Tag Team Championship over the Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) by pinfall (Without A Net).

evidence.note: The Prophets attacked before the bell and controlled much of the early match, but the Romanis rallied with fast tags; a mystery burst of ringside pyrotechnics and an extreme close-up of an eyeball on the arena screen distracted Shadoe Rage long enough for Niklos to counter a Hammer of God attempt with a seated jawbreaker, and the Romanis finished Shadoe with Without A Net for the pin.

matches.how: Tigress retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Scorpio by submission (the Marjara Mallaka).

evidence.note: A back-and-forth contest between two kick-based strikers ended when Tigress evaded a charge with a backflip into a dropkick to the knee, then dragged Scorpio into the Marjara Mallaka for the submission.

matches.how: "Violent" Victor Frost retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over Uriah Hawkins in the main event by pinfall.

evidence.note: Hawkins had Frost reeling after a Michinoku Driver and a swinging neckbreaker, and leapt from the top rope for his own Suicide DDT finisher, but Frost hung onto the top rope so that Hawkins instead drove his own head into the mat, allowing Frost to cover him for the win.

notes: Marcus Nuit again talked his way past Jessica Marshall by phone into hosting. A video package hyped the debut of masked luchador L. Dan Dee. "Smooth as Silk" Miguel Quesada, a former WWO Television Champion accompanied by valet Talia DiMartino and bodyguard Swoll, announced his own UWF debut and stated intentions to chase the World Heavyweight Championship. "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb, egged on by an unseen woman backstage, vowed to start targeting more dangerous opponents. Erik and Chad Grimsson previewed their own match against the returning Strictly Business. Chris O'Brien talked a reluctant Sam Steeley into joining him, Brian McKenzie and Keith Marshall at a strip club; the night out, and Sam's own drunken needling of McKenzie's relationship with Donna Tetreault, sent a distraught McKenzie racing to win Donna back, and the two reconciled at her hotel room door under an armful of gifts. Becky Byers thanked Sierra Browne for her own recent turn toward decency ahead of Sierra's own upcoming number-one-contender match with Stephanie Harper. Misaki Ishikawa of Team BATTLE*DREAM, through manager Rocko, refused to face "Tornado" Tara Smith, then attacked Smith and referee Tara Marshall in the aisle before the scheduled bell, drawing in Reona Yoshida, Alicia Powers, Brianna Landis and the Bod Squad in a brawl that left the match unfulfilled. The Romanis and the Prophets of Rage traded a barbershop promo and a locker-room promo ahead of their own title match, the Romanis debating their own place among the UWF's rebelling fan favorites. Tigress visited sister Leslie Hernandez, freed from the Romanis' own handcuffs, ahead of her own title defense against Scorpio. Jason Keening cut a video promo vowing to settle a long grudge with Chris Douglas by first going through bodyguard Titanicus the following week on Rampage.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own subject line and its own opening graphic agree on 27 November 2004, a Saturday matching this wing's own established Saturday Night Rampage weekday.

matches.how: "Showtime" Rick Marley's UWF Rampage Championship defense against Sabbath was ruled a no-contest after Jamie Underwood interfered with a steel chair, busting Sabbath open and working over his own knee brace.

evidence.note: A hard-fought title match saw both men trade near-falls until Underwood blindsided Sabbath from behind mid-suplex; Marley pulled the chair away and briefly turned it on Underwood himself before the referee lost control. Underwood accepted Sabbath's own Last Man Standing challenge for Rise to Power on his way out, adding a stipulation that a Sabbath win would mean Sonya Benedict's reinstatement.

matches.how: Jason Keening beat Titanicus by pinfall (a bridging Northern Lights suplex).

evidence.note: Titanicus dominated for long stretches with power moves, saved twice by employer Chris Douglas's own interference (a rope-assisted escape from a Boston crab, a distracting shove that briefly turned the match), but Keening reversed an Irish whip into Douglas himself, then countered a second whip into the winning suplex. Douglas ambushed the celebrating Keening afterward with a Dragon Douglasplex.

matches.how: Luke Kinsey beat Steve Ryott by pinfall (the Cherry Pop Drop, a double underhook facebuster).

evidence.note: Kinsey mocked Ryott as a nobody beforehand; Ryott jumped him before the bell and built an early lead with a German suplex and a tornado DDT counter, but a springboard dropkick and a superkick ("the Big Bang") turned the match, and Kinsey's own cornerman Joey landed a cane shot to the back along the way.

matches.how: Sierra Browne beat "Superstar" Stephanie Harper by pinfall (a top-rope Sierra Slice) to become the number one contender to the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World.

evidence.note: Women's Champion Donna Tetreault interfered from ringside, tripping Browne into a rollup loss that Harper refused to accept, asking the referee to restart the match rather than win that way; the two wrestlers briefly united to chase Tetreault off before finishing the contest, Browne escaping a superplex attempt to land the deciding top-rope Sierra Slice. Harper and Browne embraced afterward to a standing ovation.

matches.how: "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee and Tesla St. James beat Alex Extreme and a substituting Nina Grimsson by pinfall (Lee's own Gone To Texas on Extreme).

evidence.note: Billed as a mixed tag pairing Extreme with an injured Lisa Drake, the match went on with Nina Grimsson substituting after Drake was carried out on a stretcher earlier in the night; a returning Kyle Lee, cutting a pre-match promo vowing revenge on Edmond Winston IV, countered a tie-up into the winning Gone To Texas on Extreme.

matches.how: The Pride (Scott Daniels, Team Canada, and a surprise new member) beat Amity (the One-Winged Angel, Rage, and Spice) by pinfall in the main event Bluff City Streetfight, "Dead End" Derek Martin turning on the One-Winged Angel to chairshot him and hit a Pridebreaker for the winning fall.

evidence.note: A come-as-you-are no-disqualification brawl fought both in the ring and up the aisle: Rage was backdropped through a technician's table by Team Canada, Spice was choked and double-DDT'd on the stage, and the One-Winged Angel traded near-falls with Daniels, escaping a chickenwing submission with cane shots. A mystery attacker disguised as a fan (revealed as Shaun Borders) ambushed Tom Landis at ringside, shattering Landis's own crutch over his bad leg and DDTing him, drawing the referee's attention away just long enough for Derek Martin — seated ringside all night as a spectator — to enter the ring, chairshot the One-Winged Angel, and hit the Pridebreaker for the pin, revealing himself as the Pride's newest member.

notes: Non-match content built heavily toward the Rise to Power pay-per-view. Jamie Underwood accepted Sabbath's own Last Man Standing challenge on the condition a Sabbath win would mean Sonya Benedict's reinstatement; owner Edmond Winston IV separately agreed to face Sabbath himself the following week in a Hardcore Match to prepare Underwood, and sparred backstage with new signing Luke Kinsey over Marshall Law's own unpopularity. The Youngbloods (Allison Ivey, Michael Augustine, Edward and Jacob Drake) tried to recruit Lisa Drake; when she refused, her own brother Jacob and Ivey beat her down until Nina Grimsson, Chad and Erik Grimsson, and Alex Extreme ran in to clear the ring, carrying Drake out on a makeshift gurney. Papa Legba approached Chad Grimsson afterward offering an alliance, invoking his own past with Sabbat Justice; the two shook on a wary truce. A UWF World Tag Team Championship defense by the Privateers against the Sons of Cacaphony, and a singles match between Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme, were both set for Rise to Power. The Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage, with Marissa Monet and Pizzazz) called out the Hands of Death (Caliban, Serge Annis) over an old IIWF rivalry between Shadoe Rage and Annis; the confrontation turned into a brawl that ended with Derek Rage driving Caliban through a burning, chair-loaded table with a Flaming Godkiller, and a dog collar match was set for Rise to Power. Victor Frost fired manager Victoria Marquess after she confronted him over abandoning her and Simone Sumner; Marquess revealed before leaving that she had already signed a mystery challenger for Frost's own UWF North American Heavyweight Championship at the pay-per-view. Backstage, Brian McKenzie gave girlfriend Donna Tetreault a foot rub before declaring, egged on by tag partner Chris O'Brien and Tetreault herself, that he would start booking his own matches. The Bod Squad (Tara Marshall, Brianna Landis) confronted Commissioner Becky Byers over a referee's own beating at the hands of a challenger team; Byers set their UWF Women's Tag Team Championship defense against Team BATTLE*DREAM ("Tornado" Tara Smith, Alicia Powers) for Rise to Power. Scott Daniels worked the crowd before the main event, then formally challenged the One-Winged Angel to a steel cage match at Rise to Power.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "December 1st, 2004 - Nationwide Arena - Columbus, OH"; the subject line's own bracketed notation ("[12.01.05]") is a stray, inconsistent with the show's own on-screen date and not relied on.

matches.how: L. Dan Dee beat Brick Rosen by submission (a figure-four leglock).

evidence.note: In his own second UWF outing, Dan Dee weathered an early attack on his ribs and knee from Rosen before grinding him down with chopblocks and a corner choke, finishing with the leglock as manager Olivia Michaels looked on.

matches.how: Trevor Hextall beat "Hentai" Ryu Osawa by pinfall (a heart punch), manager Kari Stevens tying Osawa in the ropes for the finish.

evidence.note: Osawa gave up the numbers game early by tossing his own mascot rooster, Trice, to the announce table, then traded near-falls with Hextall until Stevens's own interference sealed it; Bob Jablonski and Hextall beat Osawa down afterward while tag partner Michael Bonn refused to help, until a returning "Showtime" Rick Marley ran Team Canada off.

matches.how: Alicia Powers beat Tesla St. James by submission (an STF half nelson, reversed out of St. James's own Red Irish).

evidence.note: Powers's own first match back since being attacked in Miami; cornered by "Tornado" Tara Smith, she survived a Red Irish attempt by rolling through into the winning submission.

matches.how: Jamie Underwood beat "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by pinfall (a second split-legged moonsault).

evidence.note: Embrey had the advantage for most of the match until Sabbath appeared in the ring with a Singapore cane, unnerving Underwood without ever touching him; Embrey's own manager, Farmer Johnson's daughter, then distracted the referee, but Underwood recovered with a Shining Wizard and two moonsaults for the pin.

matches.how: Brianna Landis beat Reona Yoshida by pinfall (a high moonsault press).

evidence.note: Tara "Sunburst" Marshall blindsided Misaki Ishikawa at ringside with the Bod Squad's own championship belt, then used Ishikawa's own taser on a bystander identified only as Rocko; Yoshida left the ring to check on her partner, letting Landis recover, whip her into the ringpost, and finish her with the moonsault.

matches.how: The Amazing Romanis's defense of the UWF North American Tag Team Championship against the Hands of Death was thrown out after the arriving Prophets of Rage provoked all four men into a weapons brawl.

evidence.note: The champions dominated with quick tags until Annis and Caliban began cheating openly once the Prophets of Rage appeared at ringside; the referee tossed the match after a series of illegal double-teams and a ringpost hotshot, and Annis and Caliban hung both Romanis by dog collars from the top rope before Derek and Shadoe Rage set the Prophets' own table and chair on fire in response.

matches.how: The Privateers (Edward and Jacob Drake) retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship over Fury (Rage and Spice) by pinfall (a double dropstep toehold into a flying kneedrop).

evidence.note: Fury, coached from the corner by "Supervixen" Ami Tran and the One-Winged Angel after a flat pre-match mood over Amity's own losing streak, had spells of control before the champions isolated Spice and finished with a double toehold and a kneedrop to the back of the head.

matches.how: Tigress's defense of the UWF Meltdown Championship against Scott "Hotspot" Daniels ended in a double disqualification after both wrestlers threw a simultaneous low blow and eye-rake.

evidence.note: An ugly, brawling contest that opened with Tigress blasting Daniels with the title belt before the bell over a crude remark, and closed with both wrestlers disqualified for fouling each other at the same moment; Daniels needled her afterward with a curt "Well done, bitch."

notes: Built almost entirely toward the Rise to Power pay-per-view. A vignette introduced Tumaffi, a self-declared "civilized savage" who wrecked the production studio while filming his own debut promo, billed as coming soon. Marcus Nuit talked Jessica "Fatality" Marshall into a Rampage Championship shot on the pre-show by phone, overheard by Becky Byers. Another vignette teased the still-unseen Trey DaMann, expected to debut after the pay-per-view. "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas needled Jason Keening ahead of their own building rivalry while Titanicus nursed a grudge of his own. Sierra Browne, still furious over Donna Tetreault's own interference in her number one contendership win, vowed revenge to Moe Owens; Stephanie Harper wished her well from home. "Superstar" Stephanie Harper (via video) and the Amazing Romanis both leaned hard into the promotion's own upcoming pay-per-view build, the Romanis openly baiting the Prophets of Rage and the Hands of Death over the two teams' own dog collar match.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "12-11-2004"; commentary confirms it as the final Rampage before Rise to Power, matching the promotion's own established pay-per-view build.

matches.how: Papa Legba beat Uriah Hawkins by pinfall (Roots, a fireman's carry slam) in a mutually-agreed grudge match.

evidence.note: Both men blamed each other for their own past title losses; a hard-fought contest with several near-falls on both sides ended when Legba escaped a sunset flip powerbomb and countered Hawkins's own full-nelson escape into the winning slam. The two shook hands afterward.

matches.how: "Showtime" Rick Marley retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas by pinfall (the Limelight).

evidence.note: A high-flying title defense that saw Douglas smash Marley through the timekeeper's table with an Asai moonsault off the ring apron; Douglas nearly finished Marley from the top rope, but Jason Keening's own appearance at the top of the aisle distracted him, and Marley capitalized with a low blow and the Limelight for the pin. Douglas laid the referee out with a Dragon Douglasplex afterward.

matches.how: Luke Kinsey beat Jason Keening by pinfall (a reverse cradle, with his own feet illegally hooked on the ropes).

evidence.note: Kinsey proposed a weapons-free technical contest himself, then abandoned it the moment Keening began winning; Keening reversed a Cherry Pop Drop attempt into a crossface and battered Kinsey with three suplexes, but a low blow and a stolen pin ended it. Chris Douglas and Titanicus jumped Keening afterward, whip-strapping him and setting a strap match for Rise to Power.

matches.how: Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie beat Sierra Browne and a returning Paul Wong by pinfall, McKenzie pinning Wong after Tetreault planted smuggled brass knuckles on him.

evidence.note: A pre-match search of both women found nothing, but Tetreault produced brass knuckles from nowhere mid-match, using them on Wong (who was moments from finishing McKenzie with a gorilla press) before McKenzie rolled him up for the pin; Chris O'Brien's own ringside protest sign ended up used as a weapon on Wong along the way.

matches.how: "Dead End" Derek Martin's non-title match with the One-Winged Angel was never resumed after the referee was knocked out in a wider brawl and the bell never rang again.

evidence.note: Martin's own formal introduction as the Pride's newest member, with a vow to "break" Alex Kidd; the match itself was overtaken by a backstage Pride-Fury riot, ringside interference from Scott Daniels (a chairshot off the top rope) and Kari Stevens, and a returning Alex Kidd's own run-in save of the beaten One-Winged Angel, with no finish ever restored.

matches.how: Sabbath beat Edmond Winston IV by pinfall (a Black Tie Suplex through a table) in a Hardcore Rules match Winston arranged himself.

evidence.note: A brutal brawl through the crowd and around ringside that saw both men driven through a production table, a pane of glass, and a section of hockey boards; Winston nearly finished Sabbath with a cobra clutch sleeper ("the Black Tie Affair") before Sabbath reversed a second attempt into the winning suplex off the ring apron.

matches.how: "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee retained the UWF World Heavyweight Championship over "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez by pinfall (a surprise inside cradle).

evidence.note: Lee worked Martinez's own bad left knee throughout a hard-fought main event; Martinez's own knee buckled while attempting a brainbuster off the ring apron, and Lee rolled him into the winning cradle. The two shook hands afterward, denying Luke Kinsey his own shot at the title for Rise to Power.

notes: The last Rampage before Rise to Power, building the pay-per-view card hard across every angle. Becky Byers seized the Youngbloods' own ownership shares from Edward Drake, staking their return on the Privateers' own title defense against the Sons of Cacaphony and Michael Augustine's own match against Alex Extreme, over Allison Ivey's own objections; Byers also named Lisa Drake as Alex Extreme's own manager for that match, further angering Ivey. Jessica "Fatality" Marshall clashed with Jamie Underwood over his own commitment to beating Sabbath, staking five percent of her own ownership on it, then was outmaneuvered by Byers into booking Luke Kinsey against "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez for Rise to Power, a match worth a UWF World Heavyweight Championship shot if Martinez beat Kyle Lee that same night (he did not). "Dead End" Derek Martin's formal arrival in the Pride touched off a locker-room riot between Team Canada and Fury that spilled into the arena itself; Ryu Osawa's own attempt to stop it ended with him being jumped. The Amazing Romanis challenged the winner of the Hands of Death-Prophets of Rage feud to a title match, turning that pay-per-view dog collar match into a number one contenders' match as well. The Prophets of Rage's own Marissa Monet and Pizzazz were abducted by Serge Annis and Caliban and chokeslammed off a skybox balcony onto a production table, then hoisted back up by their own dog-collar chains; Alex Kidd, Ryu Osawa, Paul Wong, and Stephanie Harper failed to free them before the broadcast's own close.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "May 25th, 2005 - San Jose Arena - San Jose, CA."

matches.how: Trey DaMann beat "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by pinfall (the Trillion Dollar DDT) in his own UWF debut.

evidence.note: DaMann demanded Embrey lay down before the match even started, then opened himself up to an early beating; recovered to grind Embrey down with suplexes and takedowns before finishing with the jumping DDT.

matches.how: Tumaffi beat Zero-G by pinfall (the Polynesian Burial, a Samoan drop) in his own UWF debut.

evidence.note: Zero-G opened with a flurry of dropkicks and forearms that did little to slow the bigger man, who absorbed an Irish whip attempt with a headbutt before finishing inside a minute.

matches.how: Moira Faith beat "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict by pinfall (a rolling Diamond Dust ace crusher) as a mystery opponent, in her own UWF debut.

evidence.note: Benedict refused a handshake and stayed in control for most of the match, but a faked hug from Faith turned into a suplex, and Faith checked on a downed Benedict instead of covering her before finishing with the slingshot ace crusher. Benedict attacked Faith after the bell and busted her open.

matches.how: "Tornado" Tara Smith and Alicia Powers beat the Bod Squad (Brianna Landis, Tara "Sunburst" Marshall) by pinfall (a 450 splash by Powers on Landis).

evidence.note: The two teams brawled to the ring before the bell; Landis and Marshall nearly finished Powers with a fireman's-carry frog splash before Smith pulled her free, and Powers answered with a leaping spear on both members of the Bod Squad and the match-ending 450.

matches.how: "Smooth as Silk" Miguel Quesada beat Steve Ryott by pinfall (a cradle piledriver).

evidence.note: A quick squash: a dropkick and a snapmare into headscissors set up the finish.

matches.how: The Amazing Romanis beat the enhancement team billed as the Damned (Hellhound, Overkill) by pinfall (the Dance of Knives, capped by a no-hands plancha from Niklos).

evidence.note: A one-sided warmup for the North American Tag Team Champions, who worked over Hellhound before finishing with Ravnos's own submission-into-slam combination as Niklos dove in from the apron.

matches.how: One-Winged Angel retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Youth Gone Wild by pinfall (a top-rope german release suplex).

evidence.note: A tightly wrestled, mutually respectful contest between the champion and the veteran; Wild nearly won with a Revelator-style counter before his legs gave out on a second Wildflyer attempt, letting Angel finish with the suplex. Wild raised the champion's hand afterward.

matches.how: Tigress's defense of the UWF Meltdown Championship against Marissa Monet ended in a double disqualification after both wrestlers shoved the referee.

evidence.note: A hate-filled brawl that saw both women trade suplexes, chokes, and eye-rakes; the official was shoved aside twice, first by Tigress and then by Monet, and called for the bell rather than risk a third shove.

notes: The first Meltdown of the post-“Marshall Law” era under new UWF President Becky Byers, opening five months after Rise to Power. Minority owner Jessica “Fatality” Marshall introduced a new recruit, Amazing Grace, over the crowd's own “you lost” chants. A vignette teased Trey DaMann's own arrival before his debut match, and a second vignette teased a returning Corey Irons; neither Trey DaMann's world title ambitions nor Irons's own comeback had materialized by the broadcast's end.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: Both posts' own opening graphics read "05-28-2005"; the second is labelled "Hour Two" and continues directly from the first.

matches.how: Marcus Nuit retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath by pinfall (a headscissors takedown into a cradle).

evidence.note: Nuit used his speed against the bigger Sabbath through several near-falls on both sides, escaping an attempted Coffin Breaker by scissoring Sabbath's head and rolling him into a cradle for the surprise win.

matches.how: Ethan de Sade beat Jason Keening by pinfall (the Ghostbuster) in his own first UWF match.

evidence.note: De Sade's father, Chris Douglas, and Douglas's bodyguard Titanicus ambushed Keening before the bell; de Sade controlled from there, finishing with an inverted, arms-trapped piledriver after Douglas and Titanicus continued to interfere at ringside.

matches.how: The Hands of Death (Serge Annis, Caliban) beat Chris O'Brien by pinfall (the Epitomizer) in a handicap match.

evidence.note: Booked as punishment for O'Brien's own unprovoked chair attack on Caliban earlier in the night; Annis wrestled O'Brien alone for most of the match, weathering a beer-can beating and a table-breaking dive, before a late-arriving Caliban ambushed O'Brien with a chain, and the two brawled off a balcony through a stack of tables before Annis dragged O'Brien back to the ring for the finish. Billed partner Brian McKenzie never appeared, having been drugged earlier by Donna Tetreault.

matches.how: Sierra Browne retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over "Alluring" Arielle Starr by pinfall (a top-rope moonsault), in her own first defense.

evidence.note: An evenly fought technical contest that ended when Browne slammed Starr's head into the turnbuckle and hit three straight moonsaults, the last from the top rope, for the pin; the two shook hands afterward.

matches.how: The Sons of Cacophony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship over the Privateers (Edward and Jacob Drake) by pinfall (an inverted backslide DDT from Erik, the Metal Meltdown), a rematch from Rise to Power.

evidence.note: Fury (Rage, Spice) arrived at ringside partway through, provoking the Privateers and drawing a stepped-up pace from the champions; a botched weapon shot by Jacob Drake let Erik Grimsson catch Edward with the finish. A post-match brawl broke out between the Privateers and Fury.

matches.how: Scott "Hotspot" Daniels beat Kyle Lee by pinfall (the Before the Fall piledriver) to win the UWF World Heavyweight Championship of the World, an impromptu title match forced by an Edmond Winston IV charter amendment naming Daniels the automatic number-one contender.

evidence.note: Lee, still hurting from Rise to Power, dominated early before Daniels targeted his back; Kari Stevens's own interference kept Lee from reaching the ropes during a chinlock, and Lee's own crossface attempt was reversed into a fall to the floor. Daniels finished by trapping Lee's arms in a double underhook before the piledriver. Daniels blindsided Edmond Winston IV with a Pridebreaker moments after thanking him for the title opportunity.

notes: Tom Landis's own advertised rematch with Shaun Borders never happened: Borders sent a diminutive stand-in in his place, whom Landis beat by pinfall; the stand-in is not registered as a match. The first Rampage of the post-“Marshall Law” era. Edmond Winston IV announced his own retirement from the UWF, brutalized Jamie Underwood, and handed the New Era to Luke Kinsey, who renamed it the Illuminati and recruited Corporate Leverage (renamed Ron Martin), Joey~!, a heel-turning L. Dan Dee and Olivia Michaels, and a heel-turning Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian). Interference from the Hands of Death and the Amazing Romanis (not shown wrestling this broadcast) escalated a challenge from the Sons of Cacophony into a fatal-four-way for the World Tag Team Championship the following week, also drawing in the Prophets of Rage (Shadoe Rage, Derek Rage); Marissa Monet and Dalbello Rage of the Misfits confronted "Supervixen" Ami Tran over a Women's Championship challenge Sierra Browne accepted. Jason Keening, still bloodied from his own loss, demanded a handicap rematch against Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade from Jessica "Fatality" Marshall, who instead booked Alex Extreme into a career-stakes I Quit match against Keening for a UWF World Heavyweight Championship shot. A returning "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict revealed a months-long angle against Edmond Winston IV and Jessica Marshall alongside Nina Grimsson, then was confronted by a mysterious figure known only as Angel over a family history of hidden "Darkness." Becky Byers announced a sixteen-man Cruiserweight Invitational tournament with a future title shot and a fifty-thousand-dollar prize, brackets to be announced the following week.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "June 8th, 2005 - EA Diddle Arena - Bowling Green, KY."

notes: The UWF's first broadcast of the leg's own next full-text pair, continuing directly from the 25 and 28 May 2005 broadcasts. A UWF Special Projects Division executive, John DeWolfe, opened the show by dismissing the women's division and setting the Bod Squad on a returning Lisa Drake; Amazing Grace won a four-way singles debut, then clashed with Leslie Hernandez backstage. A returning "War Machine" Corey Irons won his own first sanctioned match after a rooftop monologue and a parking-lot meeting with Sonya Benedict. Sierra Browne brushed off the Misfits' own objections to a future title match with Ami Tran, who beat Kari Stevens. Trey DaMann delivered a boastful promo before winning a preliminary match. Michael Bonn apologized to Chris O'Brien for an earlier beatdown, with manager Virginia St. Ursula and tag partner Ryu Osawa looking on. Strictly Business beat Fury with a chair-assisted DDT, and the Privateers jumped the losers afterward. Papa Legba retained the North American Heavyweight Championship over "Agony" Michael Augustine. Tigress retained the Meltdown Championship over Marissa Monet by submission in a No DQ rematch; President Becky Byers announced afterward that it had been the title's own last defense, with a unification match against Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit set for the following week.

matches.how: Amazing Grace pinned Mitzi Sukkora with a 450 splash (the Amazing Finish), also outworking "All Night" Wendy Minow and leaving "Long Haul" Greg Embrey without a tag.

evidence.note: Grace dropkicked Embrey off the apron before finishing Sukkora.

matches.how: "War Machine" Corey Irons submitted "Gunman" Danny Cole with the Web of Death sharpshooter in his own first sanctioned UWF match.

Ruled a no contest after the Bod Squad (Tara "Sunburst" Marshall, Brianna Landis) stormed the ring and brawled with all four competitors, and Amazing Grace pulled Leslie Hernandez away and up the ramp.
"Supervixen" Ami Tran submitted Kari Stevens with the Woman's Scorn.
Trey DaMann pinned "Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb with an explosive bridging dragon suplex.
Strictly Business beat Fury when Mike Sebastian pinned Spice with a Bad Credit DDT onto a steel chair, after Andrew Tucker had cracked Rage with a Chronic Jumble Jaw and a chairshot on the outside.

evidence.note: The Privateers (Edward Drake, Jacob Drake) attacked the beaten Fury immediately after the bell.

matches.how: Papa Legba retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over "Agony" Michael Augustine by pinfall (a Ragga Bomb), after Augustine had powerbombed him over the top rope to the floor.

Tigress retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Marissa Monet by submission (a modified Marjara Mallaka surfboard) in a No Disqualification rematch, after Monet had powered out of an earlier attempt with a badly injured shoulder.

evidence.note: President Becky Byers announced afterward that this had been the Meltdown Championship's own last defense, to be unified with the Rampage Championship the following week.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: Both posts' own opening graphics read "06-11-2005," the second labelled "Hour Two" and continuing directly from the first with no narrative gap.

notes: A two-hour broadcast joined into a single show page. World Champion Scott Daniels celebrated his own title win with confetti and streamers, then accepted a rematch challenge from the One-Winged Angel for the following week; "Dead End" Derek Martin chairshotted a returning Brett Greene backstage and demanded a match with him. Marcus Nuit retained the Rampage Championship in its own last defense before unification. The One-Winged Angel retained the Cruiserweight Championship by disqualification over Vyolynce, whose own manager, Angel, later told the Amazing Romanis backstage that her interest in Sonya Benedict was about culling weakness. Victor Frost stole a win over a returning Alex Martinez with help from new manager Roxy Mayhem. President Becky Byers unveiled a sixteen-man Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament, confirmed the Meltdown-Rampage title unification match, announced Kyle Lee's own indefinite absence with a chronic back injury, and set a forty-man Road to the Gold Battle Royal for the following week. Moira Faith and "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict, acting for an unseen man named Caine, ambushed the Love Sisters backstage ahead of their own Women's Tag Team Championship match; Misaki Ishikawa signed a UWF contract, introduced older sister Naomi as her new partner in place of the departing Reona Yoshida, and the newly-named Psychommunity beat the Love Sisters to retain. Miguel Quesada tricked Tumaffi into a disqualification loss. Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade beat Jason Keening and Alex Extreme, whose own post-match brawl with each other was broken up by the Sons of Cacophony and a returning Alex Martinez after Rick Marley stole the Mercenary's briefcase. Luke Kinsey fought Alex Kidd to a double countout, then called off the surrounding Illuminati and let Kidd leave unharmed. In a non-title four corners tag main event, the Prophets of Rage and the Amazing Romanis (the latter ambushed at ringside by the Fraternity Boys, Brian McKenzie and Chris O'Brien) were eliminated by double countout, and the Hands of Death won by disqualification over the Sons of Cacophony after Caliban struck both Grimssons with a steel chair.

matches.how: Marcus Nuit retained the UWF Rampage Championship over the Mercenary by pinfall (a senton splash, "the Statewidesault"), after ducking a Haliburton-briefcase shot and helping the knocked-down referee back to his feet.

evidence.note: The title's own last defense before the following week's unification match with the Meltdown Championship.

matches.how: The One-Winged Angel retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Vyolynce by disqualification, after Vyolynce refused for a five count and beyond to break a grapevine leg hold once the champion had reached the ropes.

"Violent" Victor Frost pinned a returning Alex Martinez with a chair-assisted spike piledriver, feet on the ropes for extra leverage, after manager Roxy Mayhem rang the ring bell early to trick Martinez into releasing a Firebomb Chokeslam before the finish.

evidence.note: Sabbath joined the broadcast booth as a guest commentator for the match.

matches.how: The Psychommunity (Misaki and Naomi Ishikawa) retained the UWF Women's Tag Team Championship over the Love Sisters when Misaki Ishikawa pinned Lolita Love with a Death Valley Bomb, the pairing's own first defense under its new name.

evidence.note: Both Love sisters had been ambushed backstage beforehand by Moira Faith and "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict and refused medical treatment to compete; the Misfits (Marissa Monet, Dalbello Rage) ran in afterward to raise the champions' arms as an unsubtle warning.

matches.how: "Showstealer" Miguel Quesada beat Tumaffi by disqualification, luring the big Samoan into hitting the ringpost with a steel chair and then playing dead to fool the debuting referee into a countout call against Tumaffi.
Ethan de Sade pinned Alex Extreme with a schoolboy rollup, after Extreme accidentally clotheslined his own partner, Jason Keening.

evidence.note: Douglas and de Sade ambushed Keening before the bell; afterward Keening and Extreme turned on each other until Douglas and de Sade jumped both men, and the Sons of Cacophony and a returning Alex Martinez broke it up. Rick Marley stole the Mercenary's own Haliburton briefcase during the chaos.

matches.how: Ruled a double countout after both men brawled outside the ring and neither returned before the referee's ten count.

evidence.note: The Illuminati surrounded Kidd afterward, but Kinsey called them off and let Kidd leave with his wife and manager, Alicia Powers, unharmed.

matches.how: The Hands of Death (Serge Annis, Caliban) won a non-title four corners tag main event by disqualification over the Sons of Cacophony (Erik and Chad Grimsson), Caliban striking both Grimssons with a steel chair.

evidence.note: The Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) and the Amazing Romanis were eliminated first by double countout, brawling into the crowd; the Fraternity Boys (Brian McKenzie, Chris O'Brien) ambushed Ravnos Romani at ringside with a Conchairto beforehand, until Niklos Romani drove them off with a springboard splash. Neither the Sons of Cacophony's own World Tag Team Championship nor the Romanis' own North American Tag Team Championship was at stake.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "June 22nd, 2005 - Desoto Civic Center - Southaven, TN."

notes: An all-qualifiers card for the following week's forty-man Road to the Gold Battle Royal, closing with the promotion's own advertised title unification match. Ten Road to the Gold qualifiers were contested, two decided by a no-show forfeit (Niklos and Ravnos Romani, who spent the show ambushing the Fraternity Boys and the Prophets of Rage at ringside instead); a scheduled Trey DaMann/Shaun Borders qualifier saw a look-alike stand-in, Mini-Borders, wrestle in Borders's place until the genuine Borders ran in and was disqualified for it. In the main event, Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit pinned Meltdown Champion Tigress to become the UWF's first Unified Television Champion, unifying both titles as previously announced. Non-match content: John DeWolfe brought the Bod Squad (Tara Marshall, Brianna Landis) to the ring to belittle the women's division and Lisa Drake before Drake, Alicia Powers, and "Tornado" Tara Smith ran them off; Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade vowed from England to win the Road to the Gold as "the Supremacy"; Brian McKenzie lost a game of Dance Dance Revolution to Chris O'Brien at an arcade; Jason Keening smashed a locker room mirror over his own rivalry with Alex Extreme, calmed by visiting uncle "Fireball" Ken Keening; Trey DaMann held a press conference vowing to change his pre-match habits; and Alex Extreme, the Mercenary, Alex Martinez, and the Sons of Cacophony drank together at a Memphis club.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: "War Machine" Corey Irons submitted "Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb with the Web of Death scorpion deathlock.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: "Money Driven" Mike Sebastian hit a running guillotine legdrop and rolled up "Long Haul" Greg Embrey for the pin, tag partner Andrew Tucker distracting Embrey's valet, Farmer Johnson's Daughter, at ringside.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: L. Dan Dee countered a Wildflyer attempt with a Russian Sickle clothesline and forced Youth Gone Wild to pass out to the Figura-Quatro Leglock.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: "Hentai" Ryu Osawa won by forfeit after Niklos Romani failed to answer a ten count.

evidence.note: Osawa was accompanied by tag partner "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn and manager Virginia St. Ursula.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: The Mercenary scored a second DDT for the pin after Chris O'Brien's confrontation with a creeping Rick Marley in the aisle distracted Brian McKenzie mid-comeback.

evidence.note: The Romanis jumped the Fraternity Boys in the aisle before the bell, knocking O'Brien woozy with brass knuckles.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: Shadoe Rage hit a superkick and the Angel of Death Drop for the pin on Jacob Drake after Derek Rage pulled Edward Drake off the ring apron.

evidence.note: The Romanis attacked both Rages with a chair immediately afterward, injuring Derek's knee and Shadoe's back.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: Andrew "Flash" Tucker countered a vertical suplex into a DDT for the pin on an already-weakened Derek Rage, tag partner Mike Sebastian holding off a recovering Shadoe Rage at ringside.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: Rage of Fury won by forfeit after Ravnos Romani failed to answer a ten count.

evidence.note: Rage was backed at ringside by tag partner Spice and Ami Tran.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: The referee stopped the match after three consecutive Oblivions left Scorpio unconscious and unable to protect himself.

matches.stipulation: Road to the Gold qualifying match
matches.how: Trey DaMann was tossing around a look-alike stand-in, Mini-Borders, when the genuine Shaun Borders arrived and broke up the pinfall by tackling DaMann; the referee ruled Borders's own interference a disqualification against himself.

evidence.note: Borders then knocked Mini-Borders out with a snap kick on his way to the back.

matches.stipulation: Title unification match, Rampage Championship vs. Meltdown Championship
matches.how: Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit pinned Meltdown Champion Tigress with the 51st Drop to become the first Unified Television Champion, unifying both titles.

evidence.note: The main event; both wrestlers came in already champions.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "July 6th, 2005 - First Mariner Arena - Baltimore, MD."

notes: Marcus Nuit's own first Meltdown appearance as the new Unified Television Champion, recapping Alex Martinez's own Road to the Gold Battle Royal win over Chris O'Brien (a best-two-out-of-three-falls final) to become number one contender to the World Heavyweight Championship on the previous week's own unread Rampage. Ten matches: two first-round Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament bouts, a pair of companion "enemy chooses your opponent" matches between the Pride and its own rivals, the debut of a new women's tag pairing, the Kindred (Moira Faith, Myra Benedict), in a loss to the Misfits, and the champion's own first defense of the Unified Television Championship.
