Non-match content: the Love Sisters argued over letting the Kindred escape with information on their kidnapped cat, Mr. Boo Boo; "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict denied attacking Angel with a pipe; Jason Keening and Alex Extreme shared a Memphis jail cell after their own Road to the Gold brawl, visited by Ken Keening, who revealed Extreme's earlier attack on Jason had been staged; Commissioner Becky Byers booked John DeWolfe into a three-on-two handicap match over a brawl he started the previous show; and the Prophets of Rage (Shadoe, Derek, Dalbello) and the Misfits (Marissa Monet included) allied against the Romanis' own interference, dubbing themselves "Intelligent Violence."

matches.how: "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson pinned "All Night" Wendy Minow with a Dragon Spike kick, then helped her up and shook her hand after the bell.

matches.stipulation: Women's tag team contest, the Misfits vs. the Kindred
matches.how: Marissa Monet pinned "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict with the Mischief Maker, an elevated Hand of God, after Dalbello Rage kept Moira Faith off the apron.

evidence.note: The winning Misfits earned a future UWF Women's Tag Team Championship match, later moved off this show to a future Rampage.

matches.how: The referee stopped the match after Tumaffi ignored repeated warnings and kept striking "Long Haul" Greg Embrey; Embrey's own valet, Farmer Johnson's Daughter, slapped him afterward.
Ruled a disqualification for Alicia Powers after Brianna Landis broke up Tara Marshall's own pin attempt for a second time and the brawl spilled out of control.

evidence.note: The Bod Squad and John DeWolfe were run off by Lisa Drake and "Tornado" Tara Smith.

matches.how: Ruled a disqualification for Vyolynce after Shadoe Rage flattened and chair-shotted him following a swerve in which two of three duplicate "Vyolynces" ringside unmasked as Niklos and Ravnos Romani; Shadoe finished him with a chair-assisted piledriver and the Angel of Death Drop once the Romanis were beaten off.

evidence.note: Vyolynce wrestled without manager Angel, still recovering from an earlier beating.

matches.stipulation: "Enemy chooses your opponent" match, Tom Landis's choice for Shaun Borders
matches.how: Shaun Borders appeared to have the match won with a Diamond Dust, but Tom Landis attacked him from behind with a snap DDT and dragged Trey DaMann's arm across Borders for the pin.

matches.stipulation: "Enemy chooses your opponent" match, Shaun Borders's choice for Tom Landis
matches.how: "Showtime" Rick Marley hit the Limelight for the pin on Tom Landis after Shaun Borders saved him from a sneak attack and the Mercenary and Marley grappled over the Mercenary's own stolen briefcase, which ended up in Borders's hands.
Youth Gone Wild pulled himself back to the top rope after a top-rope german suplex and finished "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn with a Wildflyer moonsault.

evidence.note: Both men shook hands after a hard-fought, mutually respectful contest.

matches.how: Miguel Quesada finished Edward Drake with a cradle piledriver after evading interference from tag partner Jacob Drake and manager Allison Ivey.

evidence.note: Tumaffi hid under a rolling table at ringside to spy on Quesada, who exposed and showed him up after the match.

matches.stipulation: Main event, first defense of the Unified Television Championship
matches.how: Sabbath ran in and clotheslined Victor Frost, causing a disqualification, then traded blows with him as Nuit finished Frost with the Statewidesault and left with the title.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "July 20th, 2005 - Kohl Center - Madison, WI."

notes: Recapped from commentary that Daniel Kidd's own surprise return and the Hands of Death's own upset tag title win both happened on the previous week's own unread Rampage (9 July 2005), along with Jacob Drake's own title-winning upset of the One-Winged Angel for the Cruiserweight Championship. Nine matches: two more Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round bouts, the champion's own first defense, a women's tag contest that ended in a no-decision after the Bod Squad ran in, a returning Daniel Kidd's own tournament win, a forfeit when Sonya Benedict was taken to police custody after Angel accused her of a motorcycle attack, and a fatal four-way for the North American Heavyweight Championship. Non-match content: Alex Extreme berated the Sons of Cacophony over the lost tag titles; Moira Faith, "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict and Caine Tainer cornered and threatened Lolita Love in a locker-room bathroom, with Moira revealing her birth name, Akiko Masai, and her own history with Naomi Ishikawa; Sabbath's own attack on Victor Frost was revealed to have left him scalped bald, along with valet Roxy Mayhem; John DeWolfe was rebuffed by Tigress; Alex Extreme was confronted backstage by Becky Byers and Jessica Marshall over a looming Gold Rush obligation; and Becky Byers and Stephanie Harper set a Blind Stipulation match against Donna Tetreault for Gold Rush.

matches.stipulation: For the Cruiserweight Championship of the World
matches.how: Jacob Drake pinned Zero-G with a rotating fisherman suplex, his own first defense of the title, with brother Edward Drake and Allison Ivey running interference at ringside throughout.

matches.stipulation: Women's tag team match, the Wind Walkers vs. Amazing Grace and Kari Stevens
matches.how: Declared a draw after "British Bad Girl" Lisa Drake helped the Wind Walkers gain the upper hand, then the Bod Squad (Tara "Sunburst" Marshall, Brianna Landis, managed by John DeWolfe) ran in and brawled with both teams until Arielle Starr and Leslie Hernandez joined in on the Wind Walkers' own side and security broke it up.
Daniel Kidd, revealed as Scorpio's mystery opponent, pinned him with a reverse neckbreaker.
Naomi Ishikawa won by forfeit after Sonya Benedict, taken to police custody with Angel over the earlier motorcycle-attack accusation, never arrived.

evidence.note: Naomi's own stablemates Misaki Ishikawa and Rocko applauded from ringside.

matches.how: Alex Kidd pinned Andrew "Flash" Tucker with a full nelson bulldog; "The Savior" Jamie Underwood ran in afterward and attacked Tucker's partner Mike Sebastian at ringside before Kidd pulled him off.
L. Dan Dee pinned "Hentai" Ryu Osawa with a piledriver after Daniel Kidd ran in from the crowd and speared Osawa into the steel steps.

matches.stipulation: Number-one contenders match for the Women's Heavyweight Championship
matches.how: Donna Tetreault pinned "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson with a rollup using the ropes for leverage, but Stephanie Harper convinced the referee to restart the match, and Grimsson then finished Tetreault with a Dragon Spike kick.
Trey DaMann pinned "The Pit Monster" Chad Grimsson with a modified Trillion Dollar DDT after Grimsson nearly finished him with a slingshot full nelson dragon suplex.

matches.stipulation: Fatal four-way match, for the North American Heavyweight Championship
matches.how: Papa Legba retained, pinning Ethan de Sade with a death valley driver after swinging him into Sabbath; the Mercenary pulled Rick Marley out of the match early and beat him at ringside with a framed portrait and, by Amanda Wells's account, an adult diaper taken from his home.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "07-23-2005" over a Bradley Center backdrop, and David Rogers welcomes the crowd to "the Bradley Center, the home of the Milwaukee Bucks."

notes: Two hours, posted as separate Hour One and Hour Two messages and served together as one page. Six matches: a random-partners tag pitting Michael Augustine and Victor Frost against Miguel Quesada and Jason Keening, the Unified Television Championship's own second defense (also a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round bout), the Women's Heavyweight Championship, a cruiserweight singles match, a count-out singles win, and a main-event tag pitting the Pride's Scott Daniels and Derek Martin against Brett Greene and Alex Martinez. Non-match content: "The Savior" Jamie Underwood opened the show declaring independence from the retired Edmond Winston IV and calling out the Illuminati; Papa Legba accepted a North American Heavyweight Championship match from Michael Augustine for Gold Rush; Sabbath warned Jason Keening about his own hatred of Alex Extreme; "Long Haul" Greg Embrey was tormented backstage by his own valet, revealed as Samantha Palmer and now going by "Angst," over a debt owed to her; the Illuminati (Luke Kinsey, Andrew Tucker, Joey~!) mocked Alex Kidd and Alex Extreme, and Kidd responded by challenging the whole stable to a Gold Rush match; Erik Grimsson kidnapped and chained up Caliban, challenging the Hands of Death to a Descent Into Hell match for the World Tag Team Championship at Gold Rush; Chad Grimsson and Sonya Benedict recruited Corey Irons to watch over her against the Hands of Death; Becky Byers signed Samantha Daniels, Scott Daniels's own daughter, to a UWF contract; and Derek Martin challenged Brett Greene to a Gold Rush rematch, moments before Scott Daniels turned on Greene with a Pridebreaker to side with Martin and the Pride.

matches.how: Michael Augustine pinned Jason Keening with a cradle brainbuster after breaking up a three count with a forearm shot to Keening's back, with Roxy Mayhem and Allison Ivey interfering throughout.

matches.stipulation: Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round match, also for the Unified Television Championship
matches.how: Marcus Nuit pinned "The Drunken Icon" Chris O'Brien with a Falcon Arrow, retaining the title and advancing in the tournament; the two shook hands afterward.

Sierra Browne retained, hitting Angel with a superkick ("the Double Sierra Slice") into the Truth neckbreaker for the pin; Sonya Benedict attacked Angel in the aisle afterward as she headed to the back.
Jamie Underwood pinned L. Dan Dee with the Jamie Driver, a Michinoku Driver-style pumphandle facebuster.
Alex Extreme won by count-out after Luke Kinsey, tapped on the wrist by Joey~!, walked out of the match rather than continue.
Scott Daniels turned on his own partner Brett Greene mid-match, laying him out with a steel chair and a tandem Pridebreaker/the End combination with Derek Martin, who pinned him.

evidence.note: Tom Landis and Daniel Kidd interfered at ringside; Alex Martinez fought them off before the pin.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "August 3rd, 2005 - Air Canada Centre - Toronto, ON."

notes: The leg's own true next full-text broadcast after the 20/23 July 2005 pair, continuing directly with no gap. Eight matches: a debut loss for the World Champion's own daughter, a returning cruiserweight tournament run, a title challenger's disqualification win over the Pride's own newest recruit, and an eight-man elimination main event that set the survivors on a collision course for Gold Rush. Non-match content: Kari Stevens took over as the debuting Samantha Daniels's own manager; the Illuminati cost Jamie Underwood his tournament match, drawing out a returning Alex Kidd; Brian McKenzie assaulted Stephanie Harper backstage over his own relationship with Donna Tetreault, and Paul Wong made the save; Trey DaMann attacked an injured Corey Irons backstage ahead of their tag match; Jessica Marshall turned an I Quit match into a Gold Rush handicap triangle pitting Jason Keening and Alex Extreme separately against Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade; Kari Stevens's own confrontation with Arielle Starr grew into a fourth Gold Rush tag match; John DeWolfe told partner Brianna Landis he had spent the week securing an office air hockey table rather than a partner for their own Brawl From The Mall match; taped footage showed the Kindred torturing a captive Lolita Love.

matches.how: Fantasy Girl, freshly returned from a Japanese tour, pinned debuting Samantha Daniels with the Fantasy Bomb after a late save attempt by cornerwoman Kari Stevens was thwarted by the referee.

matches.stipulation: Singles match, continuing the Prophets of Rage/Amazing Romanis feud
matches.how: Ravnos Romani pinned Shadoe Rage with the Dance of Knives (a top-rope double kneedrop) after a low blow bought him the opening; brother Niklos Romani watched from ringside without entering.

"Nighthawk" Michael Bonn pinned "Hellraiser" Tom Landis with a Skyscreamer after Shaun Borders ran in from the crowd and hurled Landis back into the ring for the move; Borders struck Landis with the Diamond Dust after the bell.

Vyolynce pinned Jamie Underwood with a piledriver after Illuminati members Andrew "Flash" Tucker and L. Dan Dee interfered at ringside, LDD holding Underwood's leg from the floor out of the referee's sight; Alex Kidd ran in afterward to help chase off the Illuminati.
Kari Stevens pinned Stephanie Harper with a swinging neckbreaker after a double underhook superplex; Harper wrestled still visibly hampered by a backstage assault earlier in the night.

Alex Martinez won by disqualification after Daniel Kidd's own Cornerstones tag partner Tom Landis and Shaun Borders repeatedly interfered; a returning Youth Gone Wild made the save, only to be low-blowed and piledriven by Kidd afterward.

Corey Irons pinned Caliban with a piledriver after Erik Grimsson busted him open with a chair shot; Trey DaMann, attacked backstage by Irons before the match, fled to the ring apron and took no fall of his own.

matches.stipulation: Main event, eight-man elimination tag match
matches.how: Victor Frost and Tumaffi were the last two standing after eliminating all four opponents; Frost tripped Tumaffi's own top-rope Tumaffisault onto a prone Sabbath, then finished Sabbath himself with a Death Valley Driver.

eliminations.note: Pinned with an Emerald Frosion driver.
Pinned by a Soul Breaker, Tumaffi splashing onto the pile as the referee counted.
Pinned with a Spinning Sabby Driver.
Pinned with a Death Valley Driver after Frost tripped tag partner Tumaffi's own top-rope splash attempt onto him.

name: UWF Brawl From The Mall 6

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "August 6th, 2005 - The Eaton Centre," both hours; announcer David Rogers welcomes the crowd to "the sixth edition of the Brawl From The Mall."

notes: The sixth mall supercard, staged live inside the Toronto Eaton Centre, joining Hour One and Hour Two into one page. Six matches, headlined by two title changes: Rick Marley won the Cruiserweight Championship of the World from Jacob Drake in a match turned Falls Count Anywhere that rampaged through the mall's own stores, and the Misfits (Marissa Monet, Dalbello Rage) took the Women's Tag Team Championship from the Psychommunity with Prophets of Rage interference. Marcus Nuit retained the Unified Television Championship over Tigress. Angel and the Kindred fought Sonya Benedict and Leanna Love to a no-contest after chair and brass-knuckles shots; the six-person mixed tag between Lisa Drake and the Wind Walkers and the Bod Squad and John DeWolfe went to the villains on a ring-bell assist. Non-match content: Alex Kidd and the Fraternity Boys ran the Illuminati out of the building in the show's own opening brawl; the Hands of Death assaulted Nina Grimsson backstage in retaliation for her brothers, then Serge Annis brutalized a non-competing Alex Extreme, throwing him through a Sears display window; the Sons of Cacaphony called out the Hands of Death and got only a taunting Unitron segment and a pyrotechnics burn for their trouble; Derek Martin confronted Brett Greene and his young daughter at the mall's own food court; Greene hosted Alex Martinez on the Greene Room, securing a future title shot promise; Trey DaMann fronted a comic CareerBuilder.com segment; Becky Byers banned the Pride, then every wrestler, from ringside at Gold Rush and named a special guest referee for the main event; and L. Dan Dee fireballed his own manager Olivia Michaels before unmasking on camera as the returning "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun.

matches.how: The Mercenary pinned Paul Wong with a second consecutive brainbuster suplex (the Payoff), sending a message to Rick Marley.

matches.stipulation: Six-woman tag, a handicap after the Kindred's own torture of Lolita Love ruled her out
matches.how: Called off without a fall after Sonya Benedict knocked out cousin Myra Benedict with a steel chair and chased Angel to the back, then Leanna Love knocked out Moira Faith with brass knuckles and dragged her off in a chicken-wing hold.
John DeWolfe pinned Lisa Drake with a top-rope elbowdrop after Brianna Landis handed him the ring bell to strike Drake from behind, the Bod Squad's own manager taking the deciding fall himself.

matches.stipulation: For the Cruiserweight Championship of the World, made Falls Count Anywhere by Jessica Marshall's own ringside decree
matches.how: Rick Marley pinned Jacob Drake with the Cradle Shock through a glass display case in the Sears store, after an interfering tag team calling themselves Debonair attacked Jacob's brother Edward Drake at ringside and Marley threw a cup of tea in Jacob's face.

matches.stipulation: For the Women's Tag Team Championship
matches.how: Dalbello Rage and Marissa Monet pinned Naomi Ishikawa with a Spiked Mischief Maker after Prophets of Rage member Shadoe Rage ran in to help drive her down.

matches.stipulation: Main event, for the UWF Unified Television Championship
matches.how: Marcus Nuit retained, pinning Tigress with the Cradle Shock after a tense top-rope struggle ended in a Rydeen Bomb exchange.

name: UWF Cupid's Revenge 2006

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "From Pepsi Arena. Albany, NY - 02.14.06."

notes: The leg's own next full-text broadcast after Brawl From The Mall 6, following an intervening link-only Gold Rush stub not read by this collection; the special broadcast recapped and billed several results from that unread Gold Rush along the way. A special Valentine's Day Blind Date Tournament randomly paired eight teams (five matches total, an opening round of four three-way tornado tags and a four-way final) for a championship opportunity of the winners' own choosing. Non-match content: a returning Simon O'Neal opened the show with a solo vignette; Kari Stevens comforted a guilt-ridden Samantha Daniels backstage over her father's own Gold Rush loss; Lisa Drake and Jason Keening ran a tag-team drill and discussed his long-running feud with Alex Extreme; Alex Extreme reflected alone at an abandoned Montreal gym on ten years in the business; Sabbath and Moira Faith were confronted backstage by manager Caine Tainer; Corey Irons recalled his late wife Ashley to tag partner Sonya Benedict at a dock before their match; Amazing Grace dismissed a reporter's question about strategy with absent partner Trey DaMann; Brett Greene was warned by a protective Alex Kidd to look after wife and tag partner Alicia Powers; DOOM! made a bombastic parking-lot arrival; and Donna Tetreault, Chris O'Brien, and Keith Marshall plotted elaborate revenge on the returning Simon O'Neal over a shell-shocked Brian McKenzie.

matches.stipulation: Blind Date Tournament, opening round, tornado tag
matches.how: Tigress rolled up a debuting Samantha Daniels for the first fall, then was catapulted over the top rope by Jason Keening; Keening and Lisa Drake then combined to put Luke Kinsey over the top as well, before Alex Extreme cradled Drake with a small package to bring it down to himself and Keening alone. The already-eliminated Kinsey grabbed a steel chair from ringside and flattened both men before leaving; Extreme recovered first and pinned Keening, sending his own team, Extreme and Daniels, to the tournament final.

matches.stipulation: Blind Date Tournament, opening round, tornado tag
matches.how: Sabbath's own Vertebreaker put Trey DaMann down for a pileup pinfall; Moira Faith then tossed Sonya Benedict over the top, and Corey Irons's atomic drop sent Amazing Grace to the floor soon after, leaving Irons alone against Sabbath and Faith, who finished him with a tandem shining wizard to advance.

matches.stipulation: Blind Date Tournament, opening round, tornado tag
matches.how: All three teams shook hands at the opening bell. Alex Kidd and Brett Greene worked together to eliminate Ravnos Romani, Leslie Hernandez pinned Alicia Powers with a bridging German suplex, and "Tornado" Tara Smith eliminated Hernandez after ducking the Santa Maria. Left one against two, Greene rolled up Smith and then reversed Kidd's own Somersault Bulldog attempt into a superbomb for the pin, sending Greene and Powers to the final.

matches.stipulation: Blind Date Tournament, opening round, tornado tag
matches.how: Dan Kidd and Kari Stevens, Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie, and Lolita Love and her mystery partner DOOM! tangled in the tournament's rowdiest opener. A rope-pull trick from Dan Kidd, aided by a Brian McKenzie knee clip, tipped DOOM! to the floor for good; Lolita Love then pinned Kari Stevens with a top-rope gutwrench suplex before finishing Dan Kidd with the Minnie Driver amid a ringside distraction from Don't Go There. Left alone against Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie, Lolita Love was whipped into a Hart Attack clothesline for the fall, sending Tetreault and McKenzie to the final.

matches.stipulation: Blind Date Tournament final, four-way tornado tag
matches.how: All four surviving teams collided at once. Samantha Daniels dropped Alicia Powers with a Pride Breaker for an elimination, Brett Greene and Alex Extreme combined to toss Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie over the top, and Daniels then sacrificed herself, wrapping her legs around Sabbath's neck to pull them both to the floor together. Left alone, Greene and Extreme traded near-falls until Extreme escaped a Brett Bomb attempt to plant Greene with a spinning tombstone piledriver for the pin, winning the Blind Date Tournament -- and a title shot of their choosing -- for the team of Alex Extreme and Samantha Daniels.

evidence.note: The winning team was promised a championship opportunity of their own choosing; this collection does not yet show that opportunity exercised.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "03-18-2006."

notes: The leg's own next full-text broadcast after Cupid's Revenge, joining Hour One and Hour Two into a single page; the show doubled as the eve of the promotion's own tenth anniversary. Seven matches, one title change, and two title defenses recorded as reigns of record from the promotion's own billing (the World Heavyweight and World Tag Team Championships) following an unread Gold Rush. Non-match content: Alex Martinez, Alex Extreme, and the Sons of Cacophony celebrated Gold Rush wins before Jessica Marshall booked Extreme into the main event; Becky Byers refused Alex Extreme's plea for help against Marshall; Colby Greene gave an interview cut short by Tom Landis before a returning Madison J. Valentine ran in, challenging the Cornerstones to a tag match; a returning Simon O'Neal taunted Amy Marshall and Donna Tetreault before his own match; Victor Frost returned to dump valet Roxy Mayhem and demand a title shot, refused by Becky Byers; Byers also settled a John DeWolfe rematch dispute by approving a Bikini Battle Royal, and closed the show setting a four-way World Heavyweight Championship match for the following week between Alex Martinez, Luke Kinsey, Brett Greene, and Alex Extreme after denying shots to Kinsey and Scott Daniels.

matches.how: "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun worked over Miguel Quesada's left leg throughout, driving it into the ringpost three times before the referee intervened, and submitted him with the Von Braun Leglock (a figure-four) after Quesada, bleeding from the nose, could not reach the ropes in time.

Tumaffi stole the title belt from ringside to rattle the champion mid-match, then chokeslammed Marcus Nuit and pinned him with the Polynesian Burial (a top-rope splash) to win the title in his own first UWF match.

matches.stipulation: For the North American Tag Team Championship
matches.how: Shadoe Rage sat brooding in a ringside seat throughout, leaving Derek Rage to wrestle Don't Go There alone until the Cornerstones (Tom Landis, Daniel Kidd) ran in; the referee threw the match out as all four men brawled.

A charging Brian McKenzie brawled with Simon O'Neal for most of the match -- Chris O'Brien and Paul Wong fighting at ringside throughout -- and was pinned by O'Neal's loaded-glove fistdrop, but the pin did not count: the booked match was against Donna Tetreault, who chair-shotted O'Neal from behind and scored the real pinfall herself.

evidence.note: Donna Tetreault had booked the match for herself under a rematch clause from her own managerial ties to Simon O'Neal, not for Brian McKenzie.

matches.how: Neither woman would say the words despite a chair-assisted arm submission, twenty headbutts to the bridge of the nose, and a lead-pipe choke; Sonya Benedict finally sent Angel head-first to the arena floor with a Burning Sunset Flip, and the referee stopped the contest when Angel could not defend herself against follow-up kicks.

evidence.note: Angel was taken from ringside on a stretcher; this collection does not confirm the extent of the injury.

matches.how: Tom Landis and Daniel Kidd interfered for their fellow Cornerstone Derek Martin, but Michael Bonn tripped Kidd and Ryu Osawa threw Landis off the top rope into Martin, letting a debuting Juan Vasquez plant Martin with the City of Angels for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Main event, billed as a mocking ten-year anniversary gift from Jessica Marshall to Alex Extreme, with interference banned
matches.how: Serge Annis drove Alex Extreme through two tables and hit two Epitomizer chokeslams onto a steel chair, then, ignoring Jessica Marshall's demand for a third, inexplicably walked away from the ring. Extreme beat the referee's ten count to win by count-out; Annis shared a handshake and embrace with road agent Joe Reed at the top of the aisle before a farewell-style pyrotechnic display.

evidence.note: Commentary speculated this was Serge Annis's final UWF match; this collection does not confirm a departure.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "March 29th, 2006 - US Bank Arena - Cincinnati, OH."

notes: The leg's own next full-text broadcast after Saturday Night Rampage of 18 March 2006. Three quarterfinal winners advanced in the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament. Non-match content: manager Kari Stevens overhauled protege Samantha Daniels's ring image with stylist Jose Lopez, rebilling her "Sweet" Sammie D; "Dead End" Derek Martin assaulted three Rising Stars division wrestlers backstage before UWF President Becky Byers booked him into an unannounced mystery-opponent match and had him escorted from the building; debuting Irish wrestler "The Skull Cracker" Michael Reilly clashed comically with a UWF office worker before his own match; "Superstar" Stephanie Harper addressed her own history with Donna Tetreault and Simon O'Neal in an interview; Tumaffi delivered an absurdist promo renaming his own new championship; and John DeWolfe paid a mysterious backer for advice on legally rigging an upcoming bikini battle royal.

matches.how: Iron Eagle 3 surprised Zero-G with early aerial offense, mule-kicked him after Zero-G missed a top-rope frog splash, and finished with a 450 splash.
After a pre-match aisle brawl and a near count-out, Reilly overwhelmed Taurus with strikes and a tomikaze-style maneuver for the pin.
The newly re-imaged "Sweet" Sammie D outdueled Mitzi Sukkora early, and Kari Stevens took over on Wendy Minow before Daniels finished Minow with a running senton and a cradle.
The world tag team champions, back at full strength after Erik's injury layoff, overpowered Overkill and Hellhound; Chad finished Hellhound with a splash.

Donna Tetreault slid a chair into the ring behind the referee's back; McKenzie used the distraction to escape a Keelhaul attempt with a low blow and finished Drake with a Minnie Driver onto the chair.
Vyolynce battered a hobbled Nuit, whose knee buckled early after a Scythe sent him to the floor, and forced the submission with an anklelock.
Kidd worked over Wild's leg for an extended period, but Wild fought back from a cloverleaf, pulled himself up the ropes, and rolled Kidd into a cradle for the pin.
Tumaffi hurled the Mercenary's own Haliburton briefcase into the crowd to distract him, then finished with a lariat and the Polynesian Burial.

matches.stipulation: North American Heavyweight Championship, main event
matches.how: Tucker worked Legba's shoulder for much of the match, but Legba countered an armdrag into a death valley driver and finished with the Ragga Bomb.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "May 6th, 2006 - 1st Mariner Arena - Baltimore, MD."

notes: The leg's own next full-text broadcast, continuing chronologically after 29 March 2006; an intervening Saturday Night Rampage is not present in the held record, though its own major results (Trey DaMann eliminating Brett Greene from a four-way World Heavyweight Championship match, a masked tag team unmasking as the Outlaws, Team Canada's return being attacked by the Illuminati, and Luke Kinsey concussing Samantha Daniels with a Cherry Pop Drop) were recapped in commentary. Two debut matches opened the show. Non-match content: Becky Byers accused John DeWolfe of rigging a bikini battle royal's own judging in her office, letting a resulting Tara Marshall title match stand once DeWolfe revealed he had inserted the governing rule himself as a past UWF president; "Firebird" Katie Smith, signed after her own showing in that battle royal, spoke with older sister "Tornado" Tara Smith backstage; a returning Team Canada, guided by coach Grapes Gilmour, was ambushed before its own scheduled match by the newly-arrived Outlaws; "The Skull Cracker" Michael Reilly ran afoul of Becky Byers after a wild night out with UWF office worker Ty; a hospitalized Angel was confronted by Tigress over provoking Sonya Benedict; Sonya Benedict and Amazing Grace gave pre-match interviews; and UWF Unified Television Champion Tumaffi rampaged through Jessica Marshall's office demanding a match with "Dead End" Derek Martin.

matches.how: Both women traded aerial offense before Smith reversed a whip, hit a handspring double mule kick, and finished with a top-rope Phoenix Splash.
Chayne dominated from the opening bell and finished inside a minute with the Chayne Reaction.
After a pre-match aisle brawl, Reilly cut off Iron Eagle 3 with an elbowsmash and finished with a whip into a DDT.
Benedict absorbed a springboard dropkick, then countered with an Argentine Back Breaker Rack into a Psycho Driver for the pin.

"Firebird" Katie Smith came to ringside to watch Marissa Monet, and when Monet and Smith brawled outside, the fight drew in the match participants and the referee threw the decision out. finish: double-disqualification
The bell never rang: the newly-arrived Outlaws (Doc Holliday, Brent Maverick) ambushed Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski from the crowd before the match could start, and all four brawled to the back.
A Chris O'Brien chair shot to Wild's skull nearly won it for McKenzie, but Wild's foot was on the ropes; Wild recovered to plant McKenzie with a high-impact DDT for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Coal Miner's Glove Ladder Match, main event
matches.how: Neither man ever retrieved the coal miner's glove; the Mercenary recovered his own long-stolen Haliburton briefcase from the ladder and finished Marley, whose leg had been worked over, with a Payoff brainbuster onto it.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "05-27-2006"; both hours share the date.

notes: Two hours joined into a single page. A press conference opened the show, booking Alex Extreme against Jason Keening in an I Quit match for Luck of the Draw 2006 with Extreme's own UWF career on the line and a World Heavyweight Championship shot for the winner; Jessica Marshall then booked the bitter rivals together against the newly-arrived Illuminati duo the Outlaws (Doc Holliday, Brent Maverick) for that same night's main event. Champion Sierra Browne was ambushed by the Misfits after retaining her title, saved by Nina Grimsson. A missing pet cat set the Misfits and the Love Sisters brawling across both hours. Scott Daniels, denied a shot at Luke Kinsey after Kinsey's own assault on daughter Samantha Daniels, battered a substitute opponent, then was ambushed alongside World Heavyweight Champion Alex Martinez by the assembled Illuminati in the parking lot.

matches.how: Von Braun secretly exposed a turnbuckle, and after both men traded dragon sleepers he drove Vyolynce down across the exposed metal, knocking him out for a hotshot and the pin.
The match spilled to ringside, where Shadoe Rage smashed a beer bottle over a fan's head by mistake; the referee, and then the bell, called for the ten count on both teams. finish: double-countout
After repeated John DeWolfe interference and a Marshall sucker punch nearly cost her the title, Browne caught a climbing Marshall with a top-rope Tornado Sierra Spike for the pin.

Left behind by a fleeing Luke Kinsey, Martin was battered with a lead pipe and repeated steel chair shots, including a golf-swing shot to the face, before Daniels ordered the referee to count the pin.
Tumaffi and "Dead End" Derek Martin brawled through most of the match while the legal men worked; Greene powerbombed DaMann with the Brett Bomb for the pin.

Tom Landis mistakenly chair-shotted his own partner Daniel Kidd while aiming for Bonn; Bonn then finished Kidd with a top-rope Deadfall DDT for the pin, while Greene and Valentine brawled outside throughout.

Extreme and Keening repeatedly and accidentally collided and briefly turned on each other before Team Canada ambushed the Outlaws with Canadian flagpoles; in the ensuing brawl Keening threw Extreme through the timekeeper's table, and the referee called for the bell.

evidence.note: Disqualification: the referee called the match for outside interference by Team Canada.

name: UWF Meltdown

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "June 7th, 2006 - Nationwide Arena - Columbus, OH."

notes: The leg's own true next full-text broadcast after Saturday Night Rampage of 27 May 2006, continuing directly with no gap. A billed Colby Greene-Trey DaMann singles match never happened: DaMann's attorney announced his client's own absence over a staged nervous breakdown and offered a fifty-thousand-dollar bounty on Greene, drawing an interrupting Madison J. Valentine into the ring in DaMann's place. In the night's other angle, masked debutante Fantasy Girl unmasked as Brianna Landis moments after pinning Tara Marshall, then attacked the fallen Marshall further with a Death Valley Driver off the ring apron and a 450 splash onto her own stretcher.

matches.how: The Kindred isolated Katie Smith for a long heat segment, but a hot tag brought Tara Smith in to clear the ring; Katie finished Moira Faith with a Michinoku Driver and Tara covered Myra Benedict with the Arizona Rattler.
Valentine worked over Chayne's injured shoulder throughout, exposed a turnbuckle for Chayne to collide with, and finished with a top-rope Air Valentine.
Alicia Powers escaped a Kari Stevens dragon sleeper into headscissors, tagged out to Alex Kidd for an exchange, then rushed back in to finish Stevens with a brainbuster over the top rope.

matches.stipulation: Singles match (billed opponent Trey DaMann did not appear)
matches.how: Greene beat Madison J. Valentine, who had inserted himself into DaMann's own billed match to chase a fifty-thousand-dollar bounty, by disqualification after Tom Landis interfered, clipping Greene's knee and piledriving both men.

evidence.note: DaMann's attorney, Allen J. Friedman, announced beforehand that DaMann had suffered a nervous breakdown after the previous Rampage and would not appear, then offered fifty thousand dollars to anyone who would beat Greene in his place; Valentine, already in the building from his own earlier match, accepted the offer and fought Greene instead.

matches.how: Fantasy Girl escaped a Tara Marshall vertebreaker attempt and finished with a second-rope fisherman buster.

evidence.note: After the bell, Fantasy Girl attacked the fallen Marshall further, hitting a top-rope double moonsault kneedrop, a Death Valley Driver off the ring apron to the arena floor, and a 450 splash onto the stretcher as paramedics tried to move her, then unmasked as Brianna Landis; Tom Landis pulled his own sister away as EMTs took Marshall out.

matches.how: Irons powered out of a Frost dragon sleeper into a standing powerslam and finished with the Lariat.

matches.stipulation: UWF World Tag Team Championship, main event
matches.how: The Sons of Cacophony retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship, absorbing a Human Cannonball and a top-rope Dance of Knives before finishing Niklos Romani with the Sky Hammer.

name: UWF Saturday Night Rampage

date.source: The post's own opening graphic reads "04-28-07" over both hours; the broadcast was not posted to the newsgroup until 16 September 2007.

notes: The leg's own next full-text broadcast after Meltdown of 7 June 2006, following an untracked gap of nearly eleven months this collection holds only as two external-link-only stubs (a 1 December 2006 posting and a 3 March 2007 posting). Four titles are recorded on this broadcast as reigns of record from the promotion's own billing, and a new title, the Women's North American Championship, was introduced with its first champion already crowned; see this wing's own registry record for the full accounting. A returning "Modern Messiah" Setzer Van Strife cut a comeback promo naming Alex Martinez as his target. A Kyle Lee-run outside consultancy, Metroplex Broadcast Consulting, hosted backstage counseling scenes with Corey Irons and a reunion with Nina Grimsson. "The All-Around Athlete" Laura Davis, a newly arrived challenger, issued an open contract to the women's division. The War Hounds (Jacen and Ronan Benedict) confronted their own estranged sister Myra Benedict backstage without a resolution. A press-conference three-way ended with a still-unidentified masked man joining Madison J. Valentine and Colby Greene in a post-match beatdown of John Shock and a returning Alex Kidd, all working for Jessica "Fatality" Marshall.

matches.how: The referee threw the match out after Vasquez swung a golf club at DaMann and DaMann answered with a steel chair, both weapons intercepted by ringside security.
Benedict finished Daniels with a heel kick into a rollup after Donna Tetreault's repeated ringside taunting broke Daniels's own concentration late in the match.

matches.stipulation: Three-way dance, debut match for Shock
matches.how: Shock sprang back into the ring with a shooting star press onto Valentine, then finished Reilly with a turnaround pump splash off the middle turnbuckle.

evidence.note: Valentine entered leading Jessica "Fatality" Marshall by the wrist and mocked her for trying to recruit Shock the week before; Colby Greene sat ringside for Valentine and tripped Shock during the match. After the bell, Greene and Valentine beat Shock down until a returning Alex Kidd ran in to help; a still-unidentified man in a full black mask then vaulted the rail, clipped Kidd's knee from behind, applied a scorpion deathlock, and joined Greene and Valentine in finishing off both Shock and Kidd while Marshall applauded from ringside.

matches.how: Martinez's own Firebomb Chokeslam attempt buckled his surgically-repaired knee; Martin capitalized with a chopblock and finished with the End, hooking the injured leg to prevent a kickout.

matches.stipulation: Tag title unification series, match two of three, locked-door rules
matches.how: Erik Grimsson ducked a Shining Wizard into a small package on Shadoe Rage for the pin, evening the best-of-three tag title unification series between the World and North American Tag Team Championships at one match apiece; the deciding match was set for Gold Rush X.

evidence.note: Fought under locked-door rules barring ringside interference; the Sons of Cacophony had trailed the series 0-1 entering the match.

matches.stipulation: UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World, main event
matches.how: Bonn dragged Kinsey back into the ring to save him from an early countout and the two brawled to the floor together in the closing minutes; the referee called for the bell before either man returned, and both were counted out together. finish: double-countout

evidence.note: Outlaws Brent Maverick and Doc Holliday tripped Bonn off the top rope mid-match to cost him a near-fall with the Hawkwind; tag partner Ryu Osawa kept the Outlaws from further interference. Valet Brianna Landis and manager Virginia St. Ursula both worked the match from ringside. After the bell, the newly-crowned Cruiserweight Champion One-Winged Angel interrupted Kinsey's own hasty exit to declare himself the next challenger for the title.
